## Snapshot
The accelerated-computing platform that sits at the center of the AI buildout — GPUs, CPUs (Grace/Vera), NVLink + Spectrum-X/InfiniBand networking, and the CUDA software moat sold as full-stack "AI factories." Data Center is ~90%+ of revenue ($75B of $82B in Q1 FY27); the rest is Gaming, Pro Viz, and Automotive/physical AI. From Q1 FY27 NVDA re-segmented Data Center into **Hyperscale** (~50%) and **ACIE** (AI clouds, industrial, enterprise, sovereign, ~50%) plus a new **Edge Computing** platform. Whole thesis is leverage to hyperscaler + sovereign + neocloud capex, where NVDA captures the compute, networking, and increasingly the CPU. The scale-up network is core to the moat: NVLink is ~the entire scale-up market today and NVDA is expected to remain the majority of a market growing **$4B (2024) → ~$17B by 2029, 34% CAGR** (MS Scale-up primer); on compute NVDA is modeled holding **~70% share into C28**, with per-GW revenue economics nearly 2x its closest peer (UBS 2026 overview).

## At a glance — product · buyer · supplier
| | |
|---|---|
| **Sells (top 3)** | 1) Data Center GPUs/accelerators (compute, ~$60B/qtr) · 2) Networking (NVLink/Spectrum-X/InfiniBand, ~$15B/qtr) · 3) CPUs (Grace/Vera) — DC ~90%+ of rev; Gaming/ProViz/Auto the rest |
| **Main buyer(s)** | Hyperscalers + neoclouds + sovereign AI buildout (compute/networking capex); top-5 cloud/hyperscalers ~50%+ of DC revenue |
| **Key suppliers** | TSMC foundry (N3/N2) + CoWoS advanced packaging; HBM from SK Hynix/Samsung/Micron; substrates/optical (COHR/LITE) |

- 🔴🔴 **THE FINANCEABILITY MOAT, QUANTIFIED — this is a COST-OF-CAPITAL argument, and it is the most investable idea in the transcript.** *"Let's say it's $50 billion for an Nvidia data center — you need a $15 billion equity check. You can finance the other $35 billion."* Versus: **TPUs are *"probably the second most financeable,"* but *"it probably takes at least double the equity check"* and *"the rates on the rest of it are higher."*** ➤ **So the moat is not only CUDA or the system — it is that a dollar of NVDA capacity requires less equity and cheaper debt than a dollar of anyone else's. That is a structural advantage that compounds in a capital-constrained buildout, and it is why the correct posture for a challenger is to plug into the ecosystem rather than displace it.** He is explicit that this is not the circular-financing critique: *"I know a lot of smart people who work at Blackstone and KKR and Apollo and they're the ones that are financing it… at a relatively low cost."*
- 🔴🔴 **WHY THE RVGs ARE NPV-POSITIVE AND WHY THEY EXIST — the mechanism, and the motive.** Mechanics: **as long as the residual-value guarantee is LESS than the gross-profit dollars from selling the chips into that data centre, it is *"essentially super NPV positive with very little risk,"* with additional upside from a revenue share.** Motive, and this is the sharper half: **without RVGs it is *"kind of an [[ANTHROPIC]] and [[OPENAI]] dominated world because they can pay the most for compute"* — the RVG lets NVDA *"effectively help other people compete"* with them.** ➤ **Fragmentation is not altruism, it is the strategy: a fragmented model layer maximises NVDA's share of total compute and minimises buyer concentration against it. Same logic as standing up the neoclouds in the first place.** He also notes NVDA is now **acquiring land, power and shell companies and matchmaking them with offtake agreements.**
- 🔴🔴 **THE DEAL HIERARCHY AS REVEALED PREFERENCE — the most useful analytical tool here, because it solves a real measurement problem.** The problem: *"in a world that is so supply-chain constrained, it's actually really hard to tell what true customer preferences are… they'll take anything."* The proposed solution — rank the deal structures, best-to-worst for the chip vendor: **(1) CHIP COMPANY INVESTS IN THE CUSTOMER** (Google/TPU and Amazon/Trainium into Anthropic) — *"as long as the dollars you invest are less than the gross profit, you can't lose money,"* and it solves the **cold-start problem** on a new chip; **(2) RVG financed by Blackstone/Apollo/KKR** — can't lose money if RVG < gross profit, plus revenue-share upside; **(3) WARRANTS TIED TO A FIXED PRICE PER MILLION TOKENS** — fine *"as long as the performance of your chip outruns the performance of your stock"*; **(4) PLAIN WARRANTS GIVEN AWAY — potentially NEGATIVE NPV, "because the better the [chip] does, the more value is captured by the [counterparty]."** ➤ **Use it as a lens on the deal flow this wiki already tracks: [[AMD]] putting $5bn of cash INTO Anthropic (tier 1) versus AMD's $0.01-strike warrants to OpenAI and Meta (tier 4) is, on this framework, the difference between a vendor being paid for access and a vendor paying for it.**
- 🔴 **THE SYSTEM ARGUMENT AGAINST SINGLE-CHIP CHALLENGERS, AND A FAIR ASSESSMENT OF JALAPEÑO.** Credit given: **Jalapeño is *"the first good ASIC other than TPU or Trainium I have seen from internal"*, delivered in *"a pretty short amount of time."*** The rebuttal is structural, not dismissive: **it is competitive with *one of NVDA's eight or nine chips* — *"to actually be competitive with him at the SYSTEM level, you need another eight chips."*** NVDA's spread: multiple accelerator flavours, CPUs, Ethernet switches, two kinds of GPU, and **scale-up / scale-out / scale-across / scale-in** networking. He concedes the lab advantage — *"if you are a lab and you have the model and you see the direction of research, that's a big advantage for designing your own chip"* — but notes the three big Chinese open-source models (DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen) are *"all evolving in very different ways,"* which argues for general-purpose silicon at the margin. **Sizing for challengers: *"every 1% share today is probably worth $100 billion"* ⇒ pick a niche, do not go head-on.**
- 🔴 **OPEN SOURCE IS *GOOD* FOR NVDA, AND THE ARITHMETIC IS SIMPLE ENOUGH TO CHECK: "instead of having a 90% margin on top of a token made with an Nvidia GPU, maybe it's a 40% margin — so MORE of those tokens are going to be consumed, which means you need more compute."** ➤ **In a supply-constrained world, margin compression at the model layer is volume expansion at the compute layer. This is the cleanest refutation on this page of the "open source is a risk to NVDA" thesis.** Supply-lockup claim for context, and it is sweeping: **~70-80% of the world's relevant supply — fab capacity, DRAM, NAND, laser, capacitor and rack components — *"because he saw this coming before everybody else."*** ⚠️ Unsourced round number.

**🆕🔴 2026-08-27 — THE RUBIN ULTRA 8-Hi DE-SPEC, WORKED THROUGH TECHNICALLY AND QUANTIFIED, FROM TWO DAMNANG PIECES INGESTED TOGETHER.** ⚠️⚠️ **INDEPENDENT SUBSTACK AUTHOR, NOT A BROKER — no rating, no PT, no model; the author states outright that *"the 8-Hi configuration for Rubin Ultra is UNCONFIRMED information based on industry checks, and the final specification may change"* and that the revenue figures are *"scenario SENSITIVITIES, not company guidance or shipment forecasts."* Same author already cited on this page (damnang2.substack.com). Filed as analysis, not as a datapoint.** ("What Does Rubin Ultra's 8-Hi HBM Mean?", **2026-08-10** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/What_Does_Rubin_Ultras_8-Hi_HBM_Mean__-_Damnangs_Substack.html) · "HBM Density Peak: Why AI Value Is Moving From Memory to Connectivity", **2026-08-20** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/HBM_Density_Peak__Why_AI_Value_Is_Moving_From_Memory_to_Connectivity.html))
- 🔴 **THE CENTRAL CLAIM, AND IT INVERTS THE MARKET'S READING: THE DE-SPEC IS A SUPPLY RESPONSE, NOT A DEMAND SIGNAL — AND IT MAY RAISE HBM REVENUE, NOT CUT IT.** The sensitivity, stated as arithmetic: dropping 12-Hi → 8-Hi gives **up to 1.5x from stacking time** (if stacking time scales with layer count) **× 1.084x from stack yield** (at a 98% per-core-die yield, on four fewer layers) = **an effective output ceiling of ~1.63x.** If all of that extra output is absorbed into additional NVDA GPU shipments, **total HBM revenue lands at ~81.5% of plan if 8-Hi prices at 50% of the planned HBM4E, and ~98% at 60%** — versus the naive per-bit calculation (price scales with bits, 10% per-GB discount → 45% of 4E price × 1.63x = **~73% of plan**), which the author argues is too simple because *"the actual bit count falls by half, but the CORE DIE COUNT IS 8 VERSUS 12, about two thirds, and the BASE DIE GOES IN THE SAME whether it is 8-Hi or 12-Hi."* ➤ **The falsifiable corollary: *"if 12-Hi HBM4E could not actually meet more than 81.5% of the required volume, this despec can actually result in HIGHER revenue."* That is a testable bar and it is the right one to hold [[SKHYNIX]], [[SAMSUNG]] and [[MU]] to.**
- **WHY 8-Hi HBM4 RATHER THAN 12-Hi HBM4E, FROM FIELD CHECKS:** NVDA has been demanding **~16Gbps pin speed on HBM4E, far above spec**, and *"the HBM4E samples submitted so far by the three memory makers are reportedly having a HARDER TIME THAN EXPECTED PASSING QUALIFICATION at that spec"* — echoing the 12Gbps HBM4 episode. With **HBM4 already holding 10-11Gbps against a JEDEC baseline of 8Gbps**, NVDA appears to have judged proven HBM4 plus a modest bandwidth bump beats forcing Rubin Ultra (**2H 2027 launch**) onto 4E. ⚠️ **Note the author's own caveat that the newly requested HBM4 pin speed *"comes close to the 15 to 16Gbps it had demanded on the earlier HBM4E"* — i.e. on pin speed alone the part *"could just as well be called HBM4E class"*; he calls it HBM4 on core-die density (3GB) and qualification path. Do not treat the HBM4/HBM4E label as a clean bandwidth distinction.**
- 🔴 **THE PART THAT MATTERS FOR THIS PAGE'S MOAT ARGUMENT: THE AUTHOR FRAMES THE DE-SPEC AS SOMETHING ONLY NVDA COULD DO.** *"This is a move that would be **HARD FOR ANYONE BUT NVIDIA**, which has built technical vertical integration spanning **chip design, optics, and software**."* The mechanism: **NVL576 binds eight 72-GPU racks into ONE NVLink domain via optical rack-to-rack links** (copper stays inside the rack), extending peer-HBM reach from 72 to **576 GPUs**; software then hides the capacity loss — **Wide Expert Parallelism** (send the token to the GPU holding the expert, so only small activations cross the network), **DWDP** (prefetch next-layer weights from peer HBM concurrently with current-layer compute), **Helix** (shard long-context KV across GPUs) and **Dynamo** (demote cold KV to CPU/storage). ⚠️ **The explicit warning against over-reading it: *"NPO does NOT make another GPU's HBM as fast as local HBM"* — Rubin local HBM is **~21-22TB/s** against **NVLink 6 at ~3.6TB/s per GPU**. *"What NPO changes is not SPEED but RANGE."*** ➤ **So the de-spec is not free: it converts a memory-capacity constraint into a scale-up-bandwidth and software-scheduling constraint, which is exactly where NVDA is strongest and where an ASIC without an equivalent scale-up domain is weakest.**
- ⚠️ **AND THE HISTORICAL CONTEXT THAT SHOULD DAMPEN THE HEADLINE REACTION: Rubin Ultra's capacity has been cut at EVERY revision — *"from the 4-die 1,024GB announced at GTC 2025, through the 12-Hi reduction and the 2-die transition, down to today's 192GB"*, with Vera Rubin's SOCAMM loadout also reported cut ~in half. *"Looked at the other way, this may be evidence of just how SERIOUS THE MEMORY SUPPLY CONSTRAINT IS, serious enough that the chip designer has to keep changing the spec."*** ⚠️ **NVDA's public technical material confirms the 8-rack / 576-GPU NVLink domain and the direct optical rack-to-rack connection, but does NOT state whether that link is NPO or CPO — SemiAnalysis reads it as NPO. Do not attribute the packaging topology to NVIDIA.**

➤ 🔴 **THE COMPETITIVE READING OF THE COMMITMENTS MATTERS MORE THAN THE EXACT FIGURE, AND IT IS A CROWD-OUT ARGUMENT AGAINST THE ASIC CAMP.** Jefferies' conference wrap: *"**NVDA appears to have moved aggressively to secure substrates, DRAM and other critical inputs, making availability an UNDERAPPRECIATED COMPETITIVE ADVANTAGE for Vera** and its broader platform"* (Jefferies · Blayne Curtis, 2026-08-27). The corpus takes it further: *"70% growth makes it sound as if **NVIDIA has already secured that much memory capacity**"* … *"NVIDIA has reserved a massive amount of memory"* … *"**We may need to LOWER OUR SHIPMENT FORECASTS FOR THE NON-NVIDIA CAMP, INCLUDING AMD AND BROADCOM**"* (@jukan05, corpus, 2026-08-26). ➤ See [[AMD]], [[AVGO]], [themes/custom-asic-tpu](themes/custom-asic-tpu.md).

**🔴🔴 NVIDIA NVHBM — THE PRODUCT ANNOUNCEMENT THE PRESS RELEASE BURIED, AND IT IS THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL THING NVDA SHIPPED THIS WEEK FOR THE MEMORY AND PACKAGING DEBATES.** NVDA extended **NVLink Fusion** with its own custom HBM standard:
- *"Traditional HBM architectures place the **memory controller on the XPU die**, consuming valuable silicon area that could otherwise be dedicated to compute. **NVHBM, built on the same technology that NVIDIA will use for future GPUs, INTEGRATES NVIDIA'S CUSTOM MEMORY CONTROLLER INTO THE HBM BASE DIE.**"*
- **Claimed versus standard HBM4E: up to 30% greater memory bandwidth, 15% lower HBM power consumption, and up to 25% more free area on the XPU compute die.**
- *"NVIDIA is establishing a **STANDARD NVHBM implementation, available from MULTIPLE memory providers**. This reduces the engineering effort required to integrate and qualify memory across multiple suppliers — giving NVLink Fusion customers a **faster path for bringing custom AI chips to market**."* To be *"validated and offered by leading memory partners."*
- 🔴🔴 **[[AMZN]]'s Annapurna Labs is the FIRST to work on NVHBM, and will support NVLink Fusion with its next-generation Trainium chips STARTING WITH TRAINIUM4 — *"which would allow Amazon chips and NVIDIA GPUs to work together with common rack-scale architecture."***
(NVIDIA blog *"NVIDIA NVLink Fusion Expands With NVHBM Custom High-Bandwidth Memory"*, relayed with the source link by Jefferies · **Conor O'Mara**, 2026-08-26; corroborated by @nvidianewsroom, corpus, 2026-08-26.)

➤ **Read it three ways, because it cuts three ways at once:**
1. **It is a fourth, ARCHITECTURAL channel in the de-spec debate** — efficiency per GB rather than GB per package. Jefferies asked exactly that: *"Nvidia announced a new kind of HBM that it says is more efficient. **Could this be part of the despec narrative that we keep hearing about** if it can make more efficient use of memory?"* — and answered it cautiously: *"When I sent this out on IB investors first of all hadn't seen the announcement and then were asking whether this is negative for HBM. **I think it's just a sign of the times of memory being so tight and Nvidia is innovating to make its memory more efficient.**"* See [themes/hbm-memory](themes/hbm-memory.md).
2. **It puts NVDA's controller IP inside the memory vendors' base die and makes NVDA the standard-setter for third-party XPUs** — i.e. NVDA monetising the ASIC wave rather than only defending against it. *"Giving NVLink Fusion customers a faster path for bringing custom AI chips to market"* is NVDA arming its competitors' silicon on NVDA's own interconnect and memory standard.
3. **It lands on the SAME architectural frontier as [[SAMSUNG]]'s cHBM/zHBM and [[SKHYNIX]]'s I-HBM** (both presented at Hot Chips the same week — see those pages): three of the four largest players in the chain are now moving logic into, or eliminating, the interposer/base-die boundary. **Bullish base-die logic content and advanced packaging; bearish the conventional 2.5D interposer.**

**🆕 2026-08-20 (TWO LIGHT READ-THROUGHS, NEITHER CARRYING AN NVDA RATING OR ESTIMATE) — A SECOND AND A THIRD SUPPLY CONSTRAINT LAND ON THE SAME SKU, RUBIN ULTRA: HBM STACK HEIGHT AND VRM AVAILABILITY.**
- ⚠️⚠️ **① THE HBM CLAIM IS EXPLICITLY UNCONFIRMED AND MUST TRAVEL WITH THAT CAVEAT. DAMNANG — an INDEPENDENT SUBSTACK AUTHOR (damnang2.substack.com), NOT a broker: no rating, no PT, no model — in "HBM Density Peak: Why AI Value Is Moving From Memory to Connectivity" (2026-08-20) reports that "Rubin Ultra's HBM configuration is being reviewed downward… toward HBM4 8-Hi," with supply constraint given as the direct cause. THE AUTHOR'S OWN DISCLAIMER, VERBATIM: *"The 8-Hi configuration for Rubin Ultra is UNCONFIRMED information based on industry checks, and the final specification may change."* Do not present it as established spec.** ➤ **Where it fits: this is the fourth de-spec datapoint on this page (UBS 08-10 VR300 · MS 08-10 tiered-SKU checks · UBS 08-14 two-chip Rubin Ultra · Mizuho 08-16 256GB HBM4e at VR-Ultra) and the FIRST to name a STACK HEIGHT rather than a capacity — and it is consistent with the 192GB HBM4 8-Hi mark already carried on [[MU]]'s equivalent row.**
- **The reusable half is the argument for why a de-spec WORKS, and it is a systems argument rather than a memory one: "a wider scale-up domain and software tiering absorb the loss of per-GPU memory capacity at the system level," so "that direction leads to optics and memory disaggregation" and system budget/value migrates from MEMORY to CONNECTIVITY.** The author's supporting mechanics: DRAM stays tight through 2027, HBM4E "still carries schedule uncertainty in qualification at the performance level NVIDIA is asking for," twelve-layer stacking "costs more in throughput and yield than eight," and adding stacks raises package area and interposer-edge I/O — so "the higher HBM density goes, the more the system has to pay for each additional unit of capacity." ⚠️ **He is also explicit on what is NOT known: "NVIDIA's public technical material does not state whether the packaging topology of [the NVL576] optical link is NPO or CPO" — so nothing in this piece dates the CPO transition. Cross-ref [themes/optical-cpo](themes/optical-cpo.md).**
- **Same note, on the NVDA/[[MRVL]] relationship, which is disclosed rather than inferred: NVIDIA and Marvell announced co-development of NVLink-Fusion-compatible SCALE-UP NETWORKING and SILICON PHOTONICS in March 2026, and NVIDIA invested $2bn in Marvell.** The author's division of labour: **"NVIDIA offsets local HBM density with system-level scale-up, SK hynix extends [the] memory tier outside HBM, and Marvell supplies the electrical and optical interconnect both structures require"** — with his own honesty flag attached, that "moving right, verifiable evidence thins out and the content moves closer to a research direction." ⚠️ **The Nature Electronics co-packaged-optics review with an SK hynix corresponding author, published the same day, was ALREADY INGESTED as a primary on 2026-08-20 — this piece is filed as a read-through on that known primary, not as a new source for it (see [[SKHYNIX]], [themes/optical-cpo](themes/optical-cpo.md)).** (DAMNANG (Substack), "HBM Density Peak: Why AI Value Is Moving From Memory to Connectivity", 2026-08-20) [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/13_HBM_Density_Peak__Why_AI_Value_Is_Moving_From_Memory_to_Connectivity.html)
- 🔴 **② AND THE SECOND CONSTRAINT ON THE SAME SKU IS NOT MEMORY AT ALL — IT IS THE VOLTAGE REGULATOR, AND IT COMES FROM A DECK WHOSE SUBJECTS ARE THE POWER-SEMI VENDORS (Arete Research · Alexi de Unger / Jim Fontanelli, "Datacentre Power Semis: Breaking the AI Power Wall", 2026-08-20, 45pp — an [[IFX]]/[[TXN]]/[[ADI]] deck plus MPWR and STM, which have no wiki pages; NO NVDA rating or PT):** *"Nvidia may go vertical on Rubin Ultra: (1) at ~4kW, staying on discretes leads to poor system efficiency and token/watt… However, VRM supply constraints could keep Rubin Ultra lateral, with vertical on Feynman."* And more bluntly: *"Nvidia will likely stay lateral on Rubin Ultra — vertical VRM supply is extremely tight, given a lack of credible suppliers. Even lateral SPS is in critical allocation across several suppliers, so we expect Nvidia will likely design in TI (and maybe ON) on Rubin Ultra to provide some relief — Given TI's abundant supply, their lead times are just 16 weeks vs IFX at 90."* ➤ **NVDA is described as the ONLY major accelerator vendor that cannot go vertical on its next part — "all other xPU players have or will move to vertical within the next 24 months," with NVDA last, via Feynman in late '28. That is a dated, falsifiable negative on TOKENS PER WATT, the metric this page's whole bull case runs on, and it is sourced from the component side rather than from an NVDA analyst. **🆕 2026-08-18 (/run-inbox) — AN INDEPENDENT ENGINEERING REVIEW GRADES NVIDIA'S CPO LINK "A+" AGAINST [[INTC]]'S "C+", AND THE MARGIN COMES FROM CLOCK FORWARDING — AN ARCHITECTURAL LEAD, NOT A PROCESS LEAD.** (Irrational Analysis — "Intel CPO Group is Alive? + Very Interesting NVDA/LITE/AEVA Bonus Papers", 2026-08-17. ⚠️ **Independent engineering substack, NOT a broker — no rating, no PT, no model; self-declared "heavily invested in the semiconductor industry."**)
- 🔴 **THE SPEC THAT SETS THE BAR: NVIDIA specifies BER of 1e-12 across a 0.47 UI SAMPLING OFFSET — a wide timing window — and it does so WITH clock forwarding, which tracks Tx jitter and removes PPM offset. The reviewer calls it "the god-tier Nvidia CPO bathtub curve."** By contrast Intel's published results are quoted at essentially perfect timing; at NVIDIA's 0.47 UI window "all of the Intel CPO lanes would catastrophically fail," and even granting Intel a generous 0.2 UI window puts it at ~1e-5 BER. ➤ **The competitive point for this page is the SOURCE of the lead. Clock forwarding is a system-architecture decision available to anyone; NVIDIA took it and the merchant/foundry challenger did not. That makes the CPO gap harder to close with capital or process nodes than the usual semi analogy suggests, and it is a durability argument for the optics attach rate embedded in this page's rack-content estimates.**
- ⚠️ **THE OTHER HALF IS LESS FLATTERING AND SHOULD BE CARRIED WITH IT: the joint NVIDIA-Research/[[LITE]] paper on a monolithic DFB laser array for NPO is judged NOT shippable by the same reviewer — power flatness, spacing accuracy and SMSR all "excellent," but RIN at ~−137 dBc/Hz is "so bad it is basically unusable for any real-world link," with the paper's own mitigating language dismissed as "Nvidia Research cope," plus an unquantified but "horrific" expected yield on a 9-wavelength 2.25mm × 1mm InP die.** ➤ **So: NVIDIA's SHIPPING CPO link is the benchmark, while its RESEARCH path to co-integrated lasers for NPO is not there yet. Both statements are from the same reviewer on the same day. This is consistent with the Kyber/CPO timing caution already on this page — the near-term rack roadmap does not depend on the monolithic laser array working.**
- **A threshold worth adopting wiki-wide from the same paper: ~10% laser wall-plug efficiency is the critical floor for CPO/NPO energy savings, with system efficiency degrading EXPONENTIALLY below it.** ➤ **Applies to every co-packaged-optics claim on the wiki, NVIDIA's included; see [themes/optical-cpo](themes/optical-cpo.md).** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/IA_18_ago.html)
- 🆕 **SEPARATELY, A MEMORY-SIDE READ-THROUGH THAT CUTS BOTH WAYS ON RUBIN ULTRA (UBS · Nicolas Gaudois, "Key Call: Samsung Electronics", 2026-08-07 — a [[SAMSUNG]] note, no NVDA rating/PT): "Our industry checks suggest NVIDIA COULD BE DE-SPECING RUBIN ULTRA. Yet, on higher GPU SiP estimates, we slightly INCREASE NVIDIA HBM PROCUREMENT ESTIMATES for '27."** ➤ **A third independent house now corroborating the VR-Ultra de-spec already logged on [[MU]] — and, importantly, corroborating the direction of the *correction* the 08-17 run made there: content per GPU steps DOWN while total procurement goes UP, because SiP count rises. Anyone reading the de-spec as an NVDA demand signal has the sign backwards; it is a per-unit content story, not a units story.** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/20260807_UBS_005930-KS_Key_Call-_Samsung_Electronics_-Implying_ROE_below_pre_AI.html)

**NEW / BEAR 2026-08-18 — THE ECONOMIC PRICE CUT IS IN THE FINANCING, NOT THE ASP.** Ben Thompson argues that NVDA's still-pristine reported chip margins omit the expected value of equity stakes, residual-value support, purchase guarantees and other risk assumed so customers can finance more GPUs: holistically, that risk transfer is an economic discount even when gross margin does not show it. The long-run bear is [[GOOG]]/[[AMZN]] externalizing TPU/Trainium with a lower cost of capital; the remaining moat is fungibility plus best tokens/watt. A true power shortage therefore helps NVDA, while unexpectedly abundant US power gives custom silicon more time to close the efficiency gap (Ben Thompson, *Invest Like the Best*, 2026-08-18).
