There is **no other major bank anywhere close to me** in terms of numbers… **but the buy side's kind of roughly where I already am**."* His expected takeaway: *"the buy side will be convinced that they're going to do **more than $15 next year and then a path to 20 bucks in 28**… **I don't think the stock is going to really trade at 11 times 20** [i.e. ~$220 on $20 of CY28 EPS]. As you roll calendar… nobody cares anymore about 27, it's all about 28… **I just don't think the stock stays at 220** when you're talking about being inside of early 27."* ➜ **A clean, falsifiable multiple argument: at $220 the stock is ~11x his CY28 EPS. The bull case here is not an estimate case — sell-side and buy-side already agree on the numbers by his own account — it is that the market refuses to roll to CY28. That is testable at the print.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-15 — THE FIRST PER-DEAL STRUCTURE ON THE FINANCING ARCHITECTURE, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHAT THIS PAGE'S OWN CATALYST LINE ASKED FOR ("Watch the first announced platform deal for the structure"). NVDA IS NEAR AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE ~$100BN OF CREDIT SUPPORT FOR A SINGLE CUSTOMER'S SINGLE CAMPUS — [[OPENAI]]'s planned Ohio site — AND IS SEPARATELY IN TALKS TO TAKE AN EQUITY STAKE OF UP TO $3BN IN THE DEVELOPER.** (The Information · Phoebe Liu, Valida Pau, Ann Davis Vaughan, 2026-08-14 21:45 and 2026-08-15 16:12. ⚠️ **Reporting on private negotiations, four sources / "people familiar"; NOT announced, NOT confirmed by NVDA, and the email tape carries only the lede paragraphs — the full articles were not read.**)
- **What is actually reported:** NVDA *"is close to an agreement to provide **around $100 billion in credit support** for OpenAI to **lease** a proposed AI data center campus in Ohio that is **among the largest projects of its kind**."* The support covers *"financing for the **first phase** of the project buildout, which will last **approximately two years** and cover **about half the total project**, and **potentially also support some of the chip purchases**."* There is then *"a **second phase of roughly equal magnitude**."*
- **The equity leg:** NVDA in talks to invest *"as much as **$3 billion in SB Energy**, the **SoftBank Group-backed developer** of the massive planned Ohio data center project for OpenAI."* **SB Energy plans an IPO as soon as next month.**
- 🔴 **WHY THIS IS THE MOST LOAD-BEARING ITEM OF THE WEEK, and it resolves an open question rather than adding a headline: the page's standing test on the $500bn platform is Joe Moore's — "is the 25% a GPU-USAGE backstop or a CREDIT guarantee?" and "judging 25%, and passivity, will be assessed one deal at a time" (MS, 2026-08-11). This is the first deal, and as reported it reads as CREDIT SUPPORT on a LEASE — i.e. the structure MS said it would prefer NOT to see. It is also NOT passive: an equity stake in the developer sits on the other side of the same transaction.**
- ⚠️⚠️ **DO NOT ADD THE $100BN TO THE $500BN. Whether the Ohio credit support DRAWS ON the 2026-08-10 $500bn platform (Apollo / Blackstone / BlackRock / Brookfield / Goldman Sachs / KKR) or sits ALONGSIDE it is NOT disclosed in the reporting. The $500bn is mobilisation CAPACITY; the $100bn is a specific commitment. Treating them as additive would double-count, and treating the $100bn as a subset would understate. Both figures carried, neither netted.**
- ⚠️ **The "potentially also support some of the chip purchases" clause is the one to watch: credit support for a REAL-ESTATE lease is a different exposure from credit support for NVDA's OWN product sales. The second is circular in a way the first is not.** The running scoreboard remains the 10-Q partner-lease-guarantee line (**$3.5bn today**).
- **The bear framing arrived the same day and is the sharpest version on the page:** Ben Thompson — *"This week Nvidia announced a **new funding mechanism to tap long-duration capital**; this sort of **financial engineering**… may build the bridge to sustainable AI revenue. It also **expands the blast radius of a bubble in the service of Nvidia's threatened margins**."* ➜ **"In the service of Nvidia's threatened margins" is the causal claim to test: it says the financing is not confidence, it is a margin defence.** (Stratechery · Ben Thompson, "Nvidia's Risky Business" / This Week in Stratechery, 2026-08-14.)
- **The bull framing, same week:** MS's Joe Moore is *"bullish on NVDA $500B compute platform"* (MS Sales · Skyler Risom, "Friday Five," 2026-08-14) — consistent with the sized rev-share model already on this page, not a new number.

**🆕🔴 2026-08-14/15 — THE THIRD-PARTY TRACKERS BOTH MOVED UP, AND THEY MOVED UP ON DIFFERENT EVIDENCE: UBS lifts the NVL72 RACK forecast on ODM results, and the UBS/Evidence Lab CLOUD PRICE tracker says Blackwell is still short at the point of rental.**
- **① Racks (UBS · Randy Abrams et al., "Taiwan Tech July Sales," 2026-08-14/15):** *"we **lift our NVIDIA NVL72 rack forecast post ODM results from 72.5k/90k to 77.5k/95k for 2026-2027E**, reflecting a stronger Q2 and **Blackwell order book strong through H226** supplemented by healthy HGX into a broader base of Neo clouds, regional clouds and enterprise."* **+6.9% on 2026E racks, +5.6% on 2027E.** On Rubin: *"APAC OCP Summit feedback points to **Rubin racks ramping from mid-Q426**… **Upstream feedback suggests chip production as planned to 2mn+ Rubins for 2026**, which should allow **compute board shipments to ramp through H226 AHEAD OF the racks**."* ⚠️ **Cross-check against UBS's own US analyst: Arcuri's 08-14 preview has Rubin sell-in accelerating toward ~500k GPU units/month exiting FQ4. 2mn+ Rubin CHIPS produced in calendar 2026 and a ~500k/month EXIT RATE are compatible — one is a cumulative production number, the other a monthly run-rate at the end of the period — but they are different bases and must not be annualised into each other.**
- **The demand backdrop UBS re-based underneath the rack lift:** hyperscale tracker revised post-neocloud results — **UBSe 2026/27E cloud sales +7%/+13% to +69%/+68% y/y; hyperscale CAPEX +7%/+26% to +97%/+48% y/y.** *"Key for companies in H226 will be **more about MANAGING SUPPLY from stretching lead times rather than lack of orders**."*
- **② Cloud rental prices (UBS · Timothy Arcuri / Natalia Winkler / Seth Cho + UBS Evidence Lab, "Cloud Accelerator Study — Aug'26," 2026-08-14):** *"**Blackwell supply remains tight with pricing going higher.**"* **B200 now on-demand from six vendors, B300 from three (AWS, Oracle, Nebius — [[NBIS]] on "bare metal" leasing at a steep discount to AWS/Oracle); outside those three, B300 access "still appears largely reserved or sales allocated."** ⚠️ **The one datapoint that cuts the other way, and it is the only spot series that exists for B300: "the only vendor who provides spot pricing for B300 (AWS) has seen pricing growth SLOW DOWN MoM with July jumping +3% vs June +28% MoM."** ➜ **A +28% → +3% deceleration in the single observable B300 spot series is the first quantitative crack in the "tight and getting tighter" rental narrative. It is one vendor, one SKU, one month — logged, not adopted.**
- **The competitive scoreboard inside the same tracker, which is the useful part for the ASIC debate:** *"**NVDA still screens best on simple compute economics** — H100, H200, B200 and B300 remain among the **highest $ per hour instances, but screen most attractive on a simple $ per hour per PFLOP basis. TPU is the closest alternative on this metric, while Trainium and Inferentia appear LESS competitive on raw compute economics.**"* Also: **[[GOOG]] TPU Trillium spot +5% MoM and [[AMZN]] Trainium2 spot +18% MoM in July, while TPU v5p keeps trending DOWN; Google has no public spot for Ironwood yet but offers it on-demand at a ~300% premium to Trillium; [[AMD]]'s MI300X/MI355X on-demand instances are available at ORACLE ONLY.** **Hopper/Ampere and older availability broadly stable m/m — "consistent with high utilization of the installed base even as Blackwell supply continues to come online."**
- ⚠️ **Framing note: "$/hr/PFLOP" is a PEAK-FLOPS-normalised rental metric off PUBLIC list pricing. It is not delivered tokens/$, not MFU-adjusted, and it flatters whoever quotes the biggest sparse number. Use it as a directional screen, not as a TCO verdict — the page's own SemiAnalysis backfill shows delivered perf/TCO moving 1.0x → 2.7x on software alone within two quarters.**

**🆕 2026-08-14 — TWO NOTES, TWELVE DAYS BEFORE THE PRINT, AND THEY ARE THE TWO HALVES OF THE SAME ARGUMENT: UBS RAISES THE NUMBERS ON A SUPPLY/DEMAND PICTURE THAT "HAS ONLY GOTTEN TIGHTER," AND MORGAN STANLEY PUTS THE FIRST SIZED MODEL ON THE NEOCLOUD REVENUE-SHARE — the mechanism the 08-13 UncoverAlpha piece above calls "a business with no margin left."**

**① UBS · Timothy Arcuri — "FQ2:27 (Jul) Earnings Preview; Raising Estimates Once Again." Buy, PT $280 unchanged (rolled to a 14x C2028E multiple from 18x C2027E).**
- **🔴 THE BOGEY, STATED PRECISELY:** *"We expect NVDA to **beat FQ2 (July) revenue by ~$3-4B (e.g. as much as ~$94-95B)** and we see **FQ3 (Oct) revenue guidance in the ~$107-108B range** (and revenue ultimately coming in at **$110B+**) as **Blackwell is holding stable with Rubin units starting to layer in** ahead of what should be a more substantial revenue step-up in FQ4 as **Rubin sell-in accelerates toward ~500k GPU units/month and Blackwell starts to wind down**."* ⚠️ **The ~500k Rubin GPUs/month exit rate is net-new to this page and is the single most checkable forward number in the note.**
- **The framing that matters more than the quarter:** *"Because many of the debates around AI infrastructure spend/ROI and credit risk are **out of NVDA's hands**, we think **the numbers are more important than the narrative**"* — a path to **$15+ EPS in C2027E and ~$20 in C2028E**, *"numbers that should keep the stock grinding higher."* PT **$280 = 14x C2028E EPS of $19.81** — ⚠️ **note the multiple UBS is willing to pay is falling as the estimate rises; the target is unchanged because the two offset.**
- **🔴 THE MEMORY-INFLATION POINT IS THE SHARPEST THING IN THE NOTE AND IT IS A DEMAND ARGUMENT DRESSED AS AN ACCOUNTING ONE:** *"because **the vast majority of hyperscaler capex increase this year is due mostly to MEMORY PRICE INFLATION, compute supply growth is even further from keeping pace with demand** — this is ultimately bullish for NVDA and as a result, **we may hear about another significant stair-step in backlog on this earnings call**."* ➜ **i.e. the headline capex numbers overstate how much incremental COMPUTE is actually being bought. Cross-ref [[MU]], [[SNDK]], [[SKHYNIX]], [themes/hbm-memory.md](themes/hbm-memory.md).**
- **Estimates raised: C2026 revenue ~$416B → ~$418B; C2027 ~$649B → ~$681B** (DC revenue **$391B / $652B**). **GPU units ~8.8MM in C2026 (from 8.6MM, +2%) and ~10.8MM in C2027 (from ~9.2MM, +17%)**, including CPX but excluding CPUs/LPUs; **with CPUs and LPUs, ~10.3MM chips in C2026 and ~20.4MM in C2027**. **GM held ~75% at least through C2027 (the Rubin generation)**; **FCF ~$211B (C2026) and ~$360B (C2027)**.
- **Mix, revised hard:** **C2026 = 61% Blackwell Ultra / 32% Rubin (incl. CPX, LPX) / 6% Blackwell / 1% Hopper**, versus a prior **75% / 16% / 6% / 2%** — i.e. **Rubin doubles its share of C2026 revenue in one revision.** C2027 = **69% Rubin platform / 23% Rubin Ultra / 8% Blackwell**. ⚠️ **The check on the $1T claim: "our current estimates for C25-C27 Blackwell + Rubin revenues are at $1T, aligned with NVDA's $1T+ backlog figure presented at GTC back in March, which, at the time, NVDA suggested was still growing."**
- **🔴 SUPPLY IS WHY THE UNIT NUMBERS MOVED, and it is third-party sourced:** UBS raised **TSMC CoWoS capacity to 130k wpm by YE26 and industry-wide CoWoS to 180k wpm for YE27 (from 120k/150k)**, with **total industry CoWoS toward 250k wpm by end-2027** as non-TSMC capacity expands; **C2026 industry CoWoS 1.59MM wafers (+3% vs prior) and C2027 2.6MM (+12%)**. **UBSe HBM suggests NVDA has supply for ~11MM units in C2027.** ➜ **Both constraints now sit ABOVE UBS's own 10.8MM C2027 GPU forecast — the bottleneck has moved off the substrate. Cross-ref [[TSM]], [[MU]].**
- **⚠️ THE HYPERSCALER-CAPEX UPSIDE CASE, AND IT IS A BIG NUMBER BUILT ON A MIX-REVERSION ASSUMPTION:** *"C2027E and C2028E US hyperscaler capex expectations increase to **$851B and $920B** from prior $839B and $906B. Importantly, we find that the **compute spend as a % of total hyperscaler capex has historically been at 55%** — a meaningful stepdown from the estimated **64% of 2027 UBSe hyperscaler capex**. If we assume the spend related to compute trends back towards historical levels, this would imply hyperscaler capex estimates **22%/31% ahead in CY27/CY28 — or $1.9T/$2.3T**."* ⚠️ **Read the direction of the assumption carefully: UBS is arguing compute is currently an ABNORMALLY HIGH share of capex, so reverting to 55% requires TOTAL capex to rise, not compute to fall. That is a modelling choice, not an observation, and it is what generates the $1.9T/$2.3T headline. Logged as published; not adopted.**
- **On the $500bn platform (already on this page from 08-10/08-11): UBS sizes it at ~12-14GW of AI infrastructure capacity** and benchmarks it against **[[AVGO]]'s Apollo/Blackstone-backed SPV, "which launched at ~$35B for 1GW but could scale to up to 20GW through C2028."** ⚠️ **UBS's 12-14GW sits at the top of this page's own 08-10 range (10.0–12.8 GW at $50bn/$39bn per GW), i.e. it implies a $36-42bn/GW all-in cost. Consistent, not new — but it is a third independent house landing inside the band.**
- **Buyback expectations damped:** *"We hear a lot of investor talk about a big buyback and NVDA may step repo up in C2027 as we estimate the company will generate **~$1B/day in FCF**, but **we doubt there will be significant new commentary on this call** since it just committed to returning 50% of FCF this year."*
- **Roadmap, flagged as NOT an estimate risk:** UBS now expects **a 2-chip version for the Rubin Ultra generation, with the 4-chip version likely ramping with Feynman** — driven by HBM supply constraints — but *"this does not negatively affect our estimates and we **do not expect management to address topics such as these** on the earnings call."* ➜ **Sits directly alongside the 08-10 MS "tiered Rubin Ultra SKU" checks and the 08-10 UBS VR300 de-spec note already on this page: three separate de-spec datapoints, all HBM-driven, none of which has yet moved a revenue estimate down.**

**② Morgan Stanley · Joe Moore — "NVIDIA, neoclouds, and rev sharing: the next big debate." OVERWEIGHT and TOP PICK, PT $288.**
- **🔴 THE STRUCTURE, AS BEST UNDERSTOOD — and MS is unusually explicit that it is guessing:** *"So far information is quite limited and **there is more we don't know than that we do know**… In some fashion, **NVIDIA will backstop the credit, allowing the neocloud startup to raise money at near investment grade**. In some cases, that backstop will **not be a cash credit security, but a deal to use the neocloud's GPU for NVIDIA's own development**. Following our NDR with the CEO, our understanding is that there will be a **negotiated price per GPU per hour that Nvidia guarantees to pay to the AI cloud**. Using that guarantee, the AI cloud can secure financing to undertake the buildout. **In exchange, Nvidia gets a share of revenue above the negotiated backstop price; how much is unclear.**"* On enforcement: *"we think Nvidia would **get access to the GPUs in the event the backstop is triggered — similar to how the contract with [[CRWV]] functions, but with more upside potential to Nvidia**."*
- **🔴 THE SIZING, WHICH IS THE REASON THE NOTE MATTERS:** *"Our tech teams estimate the **big 4 hyperscalers will bring on ~25GW of compute in 2027 ex TPU**; a neocloud ecosystem of a similar size **monetizing at $20 million per MW (in-line with [[NBIS]] commentary on new deals)** would generate **$500bn of annual revenue** — if Nvidia captured **1/4th of that as 100% margin revenue**, it would drive **60% upside to our FY28 EBIT estimates, or 25% upside to FY29** without any change to Nvidia's initial sales. **But at smaller scale (2-5GW) we could start to see ~10% or so uplift to EPS.**"* ⚠️ **Size the assumption before the answer: the headline requires a neocloud ecosystem the same size as the entire big-4 buildout AND a 25% revenue capture. The 2-5GW / ~10% EPS case is the one worth carrying as a base — MS itself brackets it that way. Note also $20M/MW = $20bn/GW of ANNUAL revenue, which is a revenue-per-GW figure and must NOT be mixed with this page's $/GW CAPEX anchors (`ai-dc-power-gw` in [assumptions.md](_meta/assumptions.md)).**
- **WHY NVDA IS DOING IT — three reasons, and the first is the interesting one:** *"(1) **hyperscalers are not investing enough to keep up with token demand because of fcf concerns**, (2) hyperscalers **can't get land power shell outside the US** and are increasingly getting pressure in the US so the world needs new spenders, and (3) the structure here will drive **tens of billions of annuity revenue with limited downside**."* And the mechanism inside (1): *"even with the rapid pace of investment and cash deficit, **compute is simply not keeping pace with token growth, forcing customers to redeploy compute originally earmarked for TRAINING into INFERENCE**."*
- **🔴 THE GEOPOLITICAL LEG, which is net-new framing on this page:** *"As land, space and power becomes limited in the US, and large US CSPs look for permission to build data centers in other countries, **some of the other countries are starting to realize that the space and power that they can offer can be important and strategic for AI. That drives countries to try to PRESERVE those resources for their country**, which drives startup activity."* Named examples: **Yotta, YTL, SK Telecom.** ➜ **The neocloud/sovereign push is being framed as a consequence of host-country resource nationalism, not just of NVDA's demand engineering.**
- **⚠️ MS STATES THE BEAR CASE AGAINST ITSELF, AND IT IS THE SAME ONE UNCOVERALPHA MADE ON 08-13:** *"the more cynical view is it is simply **creating artificial demand from customers without the scale to use asic or AMD**, but **it only works if compute demand is ahead of supply**"*; and *"In a **compute oversupply situation**, if that should emerge, **the situation could be challenging**."* MS asks for *"a high degree of transparency in the way that NVIDIA presents these deals."* ➜ **Both sides of this page now agree on the FALSIFICATION TEST and it is a single variable: whether compute stays short. The bull sizes the upside at 10-60% of EBIT; the bear says the structure has no margin left the moment the shortage ends. Neither claim is testable at the 08-26 print; it is a 2027-28 question.**
- **THE DOWNSIDE HEDGE MS PUTS ON IT, and it is the genuinely novel part:** *"the risk is **NOT a pure credit** but rather **gives NVDA['s] development team access to less expensive GPU rentals**… in the downside case, **Nvidia can use those GPUs to push further into the market for model services or internal R&D**. Nvidia has been a very strong model developer since the invention of LLMs, but has not pushed toward the frontier in recent years."* Current flagship cited: **Nemotron 3 Ultra** (UBS separately flags **Nemotron 3.5** traction as a possible call topic). ➜ **A backstop that converts into cheap internal compute is a materially different risk profile from a credit guarantee — this is the strongest available rebuttal to the circularity bear, and it is untested.**
- **Scale context for the segment: public neoclouds are "somewhere in the 6% range of global cloud capex"** (MS basket: CRWV ex-CIP, [[NBIS]], IREN, BRUN, SHAZ) — *"before including sovereign clouds, and private companies."* Desk framing: *"Though further **'polarizing' to stock sentiment** given concerns around more 'circularity', Joe is **firmly bullish**"* (MS TMT sales · Thomas Wigg, 2026-08-14 — sales commentary, not Research).

**🆕🔴 2026-08-13 — THE SUPPLIER/BUYER RELATIONSHIP IS OVER: EACH SIDE IS NOW TRYING TO COMMODITISE THE OTHER'S LAYER, AND NVDA'S ~75% GROSS MARGIN IS THE THING THE ECOSYSTEM IS ORGANISING AGAINST.** (UncoverAlpha, 2026-08-13 — **independent paid Substack research (Rihard Jarc), NOT a bank: no rating, no PT, no estimates.** The single most quotable statement of the structural-competition case this page carries.)

- **🔴 The frame, verbatim:** *"The relationship between Nvidia and the big hyperscalers Amazon, Google, and Microsoft was once very clear and friendly, where one was a supplier and the other three were buyers. I believe **that era is clearly over, as each is trying to commoditize the layer the other serves**."* And the stakes: *"You have Nvidia's Jensen Huang with the strongest balance sheet in semiconductor history and a **~75% gross margin** business. On the other side are the three biggest Nvidia customers — Amazon, Microsoft, and Google — who together will spend **around $600B in CapEx this year** and have all come to the same conclusion: **they do not want to keep paying Nvidia's margin forever**."*
- **🔴 WHY NOW, three reasons given: (1) the shift to an INFERENCE-LED market; (2) the historic-high 75% GM, which "is bothering the data center ecosystem because it's long-term hurting their margin"; (3) scale — "hundreds of billions, and maybe even soon trillions, per year will be spent on AI chips, and every layer of the AI stack wants to capture as much value as possible."**
- **✅ WHAT NVDA STILL OWNS, stated plainly: in TRAINING, "Nvidia's share of the merchant market is still estimated to be north of 90%; the only real competitive chip that comes close is Google's TPU (mostly because of Google's interconnect and clustering capabilities)"** — moat named as CUDA + NVLink + the networking stack, because the whole cluster works as one.
- **⚠️ WHY INFERENCE IS A DIFFERENT FIGHT — the mechanism, not the slogan:** inference *"is massively parallel but doesn't need the same tight cluster coherence as training. **The workload is known and stable, which is exactly the situation in which a CUSTOM ASIC (a chip designed for one task) often BEATS a general-purpose GPU [on] cost per token**."* And the volume is going there: **[[MSFT]] processed OVER 100 TRILLION TOKENS IN A QUARTER IN 2025, UP 5x Y/Y; [[GOOG]] cited 22 BILLION TOKENS PROCESSED PER MINUTE across Alphabet's APIs.** ➜ **Read against this page's own Jevons/token-growth bull rows (MS Byrd 06-26, JPM 06-16): the same token explosion that is bullish for volume is precisely what makes a workload stable enough to ASIC. Both readings are now on the page; neither is netted.**
- **🔴 THE ASIC SCOREBOARD BY HYPERSCALER — the most complete single-source tally this page carries:**
  - **[[GOOG]] furthest ahead in chip design — "Google produces +3 million TPUs annually."** The [[ANTHROPIC]] deal signed last October gives access to **up to 1M TPUs, "bringing well over a gigawatt of capacity online in 2026,"** and in April this year was **expanded with [[AVGO]] to roughly 3.5 ADDITIONAL GIGAWATTS of next-gen TPU capacity starting 2027**. The category-changing step: ***"Google is also now selling TPU systems to external customers as hardware. Essentially doing the same thing Nvidia's core business is."*** ⚠️ With Gemini seen as having fallen behind and the AI-lab team in "a refocus period," the author argues the likelihood of Google pushing **more** capacity into GCP and TPUs to outside customers has only **increased** — a second-order read most bulls treat the other way.
  - **[[AMZN]] — "Amazon's chips business (Trainium + Graviton) now runs at OVER $25B IN ANNUALIZED REVENUE, growing TRIPLE DIGITS. Graviton is used by 98% of the top 1,000 EC2 customers. Project Rainier — the Anthropic cluster — is scaling from 500,000+ Trainium chips toward 1M."** ⚠️ The dangerous part is the margin policy, not the silicon: Amazon *"often likes to drive margins to zero during adoption periods… **Trainium, given how young the project is, is highly competitive with Nvidia on a COST-PER-TOKEN basis; much of this is due to Amazon pushing for very low margins.** There is a reason why Anthropic likes Trainium for inference tasks."*
  - **[[MSFT]] still the laggard but moving — per The Information: Maia 300 unveiled "as soon as September," negotiating TSMC capacity for MORE THAN 300,000 CHIPS FOR DELIVERY IN 2027, an eventual target of OVER 1 MILLION UNITS and, per an Azure Maia manager, "gigawatts' worth" of Maia. Context that sizes how early it is: Maia 200 (launched January 2026, TSMC 3nm, 140B+ transistors) has shipped only in the TENS OF THOUSANDS and sits in two US data centers. Reports mention a targeted COST ADVANTAGE OF 30-40% vs Nvidia chips, and Microsoft is actively courting [[ANTHROPIC]] as anchor customer.**
- **🔴 THE CUSTOMER-CONCENTRATION TWIST: [[ANTHROPIC]] — "the biggest success story from the AI perspective" — "has notoriously built most of its chip-usage stack on Google's TPUs and Amazon's Trainium (not Nvidia)," with even Mythos (Fable) "rumored to be mostly TPUs and served on Trainium, though this is also changing with some new Nvidia deals." The strategic read: *"Even with Nvidia now trying hard to offer its chips to Anthropic in its deal announcements, it's clear Anthropic doesn't want to drop off TPUs and Trainium. Instead, they want AS MANY OPTIONS AS POSSIBLE AND TO DRIVE PRICES DOWN, which is exactly the scenario Nvidia doesn't want."*** ➜ **Independent corroboration of the 07-28 Anthropic expert call already on this page (TPU "at less than half the price," "80% of performance for 40% of the price is still a very strong TCO") — two unrelated sources, same conclusion, from the account that is simultaneously the fastest-growing lab.**
- **⚠️ THE Q2-CALL LANGUAGE, read as an OPTION rather than a commitment:** all three hyperscalers plus [[META]] committed to long-lead-time capex (land, shells, power, cooling — *"assets [that] last 15-25 years"*) years in advance, but said they buy the chips, *"the short-lived assets,"* only months before a datacenter comes online. Amy Hood ([[MSFT]]): *"if the demand environment changes, you just slow down what is, in fact, the largest component."* Anat Ashkenazi ([[GOOG]]): *"Google will keep investing as long as we see an attractive return on that investment."* Jassy talked of *"different capital cycles"* for land/power vs chips. ➜ **The Hood quote is already on this page inside the 08-10 $500bn row; what UncoverAlpha adds is that ALL FOUR used the same framing, and the explicit template they are copying: "essentially copy the playbook on the CPU book with Graviton, where Amazon's own Graviton chip now handles most of the CPU workloads in AWS." All the hyperscalers are also going DIRECT TO MEMORY MANUFACTURERS to secure capacity.**
- **✅ NVDA'S COUNTER-MOVE, as the author reads it — "manufacture demand outside the hyperscalers":** NVDA is *"on track to generate roughly **$100B+ of annual free cash flow** at current rates"* and deploys it so that *"**when the hyperscalers exercise their option to buy less, someone else is willing to buy more**."* The ladder assembled in one place: the **Sep-2025 $6.3B commitment to buy back any unsold [[CRWV]] capacity through April 2032** plus a **parallel $1.5B Lambda deal**; a **$2B equity injection into CoreWeave in January 2026** ("Nvidia became the equity holder, the demand backstop, the customer of last resort"); the **2026-07-01 "AI Compute Partnership"** formalising rent-back-at-a-fixed-rate so lenders will finance neocloud buildouts, in exchange for a share of cloud revenue — **first joiners Firmus (up to 170,000 GPUs in Batam, Indonesia) and Sharon AI (40,000 GB300s in Australia)**; the **08-10 $500B platform, on which "Jensen [said] that Nvidia retains the option to backstop up to $125B, or 25%, of those deals"**; reported talks to **backstop up to $250B of [[OPENAI]] compute leases at the SB Energy 10GW Ohio campus and finance ~$350B of OpenAI chip purchases**; and **$18.6B invested into private companies and infrastructure funds in Q1 FY27 alone**, with the filing admitting some investees *"may indirectly purchase or use our products."* 🔴 **THE $125B / 25% DOLLAR FIGURE IS NET-NEW TO THIS PAGE — it is the first quantification of the "up to 25% residual support mechanism" logged on 08-11 from MS/BofA, who both gave the percentage without the dollar amount.**
- **🔴⚠️ THE BEAR PUNCHLINE ON THE NEOCLOUD STRUCTURE, and it is a cleaner version of the circularity argument than the sell-side's:** *"when we have a compute shortage on paper, things mostly work out, but **the moment we don't have that shortage anymore, a business that pays Nvidia list price for chips and then pays Nvidia a percentage of its revenue on top is a business with NO MARGIN LEFT**."* Supporting expert colour (AlphaSense, former Nebius employee): *"**Firmus was almost going bankrupt**… When one of the major partners on Nvidia is actually struggling, NVIDIA will try to help the partner and find solutions together"* — i.e. **the neoclouds taking the revenue-share deal are seen as the weakest ones**; and *"**NeoCloud, they hate this model**, so I can tell you directly… NVIDIA has a huge leverage on them, and at the same time **they paid a far higher price** to have… the GPUs. You don't have the high discounts of buying in bulk… and at the same time NVIDIA has also control on how you [run] the cloud."* ➜ **This is the specific falsification test for the 08-11 revenue-share upside line (MS: a 35% share = >$10bn/GW/yr at 100% GM): it holds only while compute is short. Also note the author's own view that NVDA would PREFER neoclouds serve smaller, diversified customers rather than do big offloading deals with hyperscalers — while the neoclouds prefer the hyperscaler deals because they move the stock.**
- **⚠️ Flagged without numbers, but they widen the option set:** [[AMD]]'s OpenAI deal (**6GW of MI-series deployment with equity warrants attached**) and the **[[AVGO]]/OpenAI 10GW custom program** *"give buyers even more options,"* plus SRAM players like [[CEREBRAS]]. And a testable prediction on [[SPCX]]: given *"the recent commentary from SpaceX about going 'Nvidia exclusive,'"* the author expects **a backstop or straight-up equity deal brewing between SpaceX and Nvidia** — check that against this page's 08-04 SPCX primary-transcript row and SIG's 08-12 ~6GW haircut.
- ⚠️ **SCOPE LIMIT: this is a PAID post and the extract ends at the paywall. The second half — "Why does a potential monopolist need to finance its own demand?" and the author's positioning conclusion — is NOT in the source read here. Do not assume the conclusion; nothing above is a rating, a PT or an estimate.** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/Nvidia_and_the_Hyperscalers_High_Stakes_Poker_Game.html)

**🆕 2026-08-12 — INTO THE 2026-08-26 PRINT: SUSQUEHANNA RAISES DC ESTIMATES TO >$1.1T THROUGH CY27 AND FLAGS THAT THE ">$1T BLACKWELL+RUBIN" TARGET NOW EXCLUDES SEVERAL PRODUCT LINES THAT DID NOT EXIST WHEN IT WAS SET.** (SIG / William Hearon, "SIGnature Preview: Demand Visibility Strengthens Ahead of Rubin Launch", **Positive, PT $275**, price ref $217.50, 2026-08-12.)

- **The print is Wednesday 2026-08-26.** SIG expects **better results and guidance as GB300 continues to ramp with Vera Rubin layering on from 2H26**, and keeps **Positive, PT $275 (~30x C2026E EV/NOPAT)**, downside risk $150.
- **🔴 THE ESTIMATE RAISE AND WHY: "NVIDIA reiterated its >$1T target for combined Blackwell/Rubin revenue in CY25-CY27. In addition, NEW PRODUCT LINES are now expected to add material upside to this figure (i.e. Vera CPU rack, Groq LPX rack, storage rack, etc.). Accordingly, we are increasing our DC estimates and now modeling ~$1.1T revenue through CY27."** ⚠️ **The specific unbundling matters: NVDA has "visibility into ~$20B of standalone Vera CPU revenue in 2026 alone," of which SIG estimates ~$10B is standalone CPU RACKS. The >$1T target was set on accelerators; the rack-level and CPU-level lines are incremental to it. Read every future "on track for >$1T" statement as a floor, not a forecast.**
- **🔴 THE SPACEX DATAPOINT, AND SIG HAIRCUTS IT — this is the cleanest sell-side pushback on the [[SPCX]] 10GW claim this wiki carries:** *"SpaceX **exclusively committed to NVIDIA** for its AI infrastructure, including its upcoming Vera Rubin architecture. Interestingly, SpaceX discussed rapidly scaling compute capacity from **roughly 2 GW around the end of 2026 toward 10 GW by the end of 2027**, a positive for NVIDIA as the buildout should drive significant incremental demand (**though we believe this is closer to ~6GW vs. ~10GW**)."* ➜ **Log the ~6GW haircut explicitly against the 10GW figure on [[SPCX]] and in the datacenter-buildout theme; it is a 40% cut to the headline by a house that is Positive on NVDA and therefore has no incentive to shade it down.**
- **Other demand marks in the preview:** **SSI signed a long-term partnership with NVIDIA to expand compute capacity by an "order of magnitude" using Vera Rubin systems**; **Sovereign AI revenue +80%+ y/y**, NVDA AI infrastructure deployed across **~40 countries representing ~$50T of GDP**, with the **HUMAIN / Saudi PIF** partnership covering *"several hundred thousand"* GPUs over five years; **top-five hyperscalers expected to nearly DOUBLE capex in 2026, with 2027 capex expected to exceed $1T (>40% y/y growth)**.
- **The hyperscaler capex marks SIG is using (useful as a consensus check against this wiki's own numbers):** **[[GOOG]]** 2Q capex **$44.9bn** vs Street $44.8bn, FY26 guide **raised to $195–205bn from $180–190bn**; **[[MSFT]]** quarterly PP&E **$36.6bn vs Street $42.2bn** — the shortfall attributed to *"timing and classification of data center investments rather than weaker underlying demand"* — with **>$50bn expected in 3Q (+45% q/q)** and FY26 **~$175bn vs prior Street ~$190bn**, the reduction *"primarily reflect[ing] a shift in data center leases from finance to operating leases"*; **[[META]]** FY26 capex guided **$130–145bn**, narrowed from $125bn+. ⚠️ **Note both MSFT "cuts" are accounting/classification effects, not demand — worth carrying because the headline numbers read as reductions.**
- **⚠️ TWO CAUTIONS FROM A BULL, and they are the ones to watch into the print:** (1) **Gross margin — "we expect generally in-line GMs for July. While management is 'working' to maintain GMs in the mid-70s for the year, GMs may be PRESSURED IN THE BACK HALF as Rubin first launches."** (2) **China — "while recent reports suggest NVIDIA may be selling limited H200 AI chips to China, we continue to EXCLUDE China revenue in our model as the regulatory backdrop remains fluid."** ➜ **China is optionality not in the numbers; Rubin launch margin is the near-term risk.**
- **✅ Supply framing that supports pricing: Rubin remains on track for a 2H26 launch (first samples shipped to customers in late February), and management expects the chip to be SUPPLY CONSTRAINED THROUGHOUT ITS ENTIRE LIFE CYCLE.**
- **Independent framing on the same day, and it is the sharpest one-line statement of the [[CRWV]]/[[NBIS]] financing story from NVDA's side: "Nvidia Is Speedrunning the Creation of a Synthetic Hyperscaler"** (Tae Kim, Key Context, 2026-08-12 — independent newsletter, not sell-side). Cross-ref the $500bn platform mechanics logged below and the [[CRWV]]/[[NBIS]] prints of 08-11/08-12.
- **Desk flow:** MS TMT led with **"Bullish AI earnings + NVDA A100 deal"** (Tom Wigg, 2026-08-12); BofA's morning note flagged **"TABLE-POUNDING on AI, NVIDIA Access"** (Nicholas Villani, 2026-08-12); The Information ran **"Nvidia's Stargate power bet"** (2026-08-12). *(Desk/press commentary, not Research.)*

**🆕🔴 2026-08-11 — THE $500BN PLATFORM'S ACTUAL MECHANICS LANDED, AND THEY ARE BETTER THAN THE HEADLINE: NVDA IS UNDERWRITING RESIDUAL VALUE ON UP TO 25% OF DEALS, NOT THE LOANS. The whole sell-side moved to "net positive," and the stock fell -2.9% on 08-10 and went flat on 08-11 anyway.**

- **🔴 The disclosure that changes the risk read (Morgan Stanley / Joseph Moore, OW, PT $288, 2026-08-11):** NVDA mobilised **$500bn of *potential* investment from 6 institutional partners** to form *"independent compute financing platforms"*; **the partners evaluate each opportunity on its merits and no decisions have been made yet**; NVDA provides ecosystem support and *may* provide a **"residual support mechanism" for up to 25% of the investments**, which in the company's words is *"**limited, residual value based, and designed to complement — not replace — independent underwriting**."*
- **🔴 The base-rate that should anchor the circularity debate, and it is small:** *"NVIDIA's actual direct credit exposure thus far is mostly confined to credit backstops with a couple of smaller neoclouds. **Nvidia's most recent 10-Q quantifies total exposure to partner lease guarantees at $3.5bn**"* — the equity investments in customers/partners are *"equity investments, not donations or backstops"* (MS / Moore, 2026-08-11). BofA sizes the *whole* prior vendor-financing programme (incl. the [[OPENAI]] initial $100bn and ~$250bn guarantee) at only **~15% of ~$470bn of FCF over CY26–27** (BofA / Vivek Arya, 2026-08-11).
- **🔴 The upside nobody was modelling — a 100%-gross-margin annuity.** Moore: using MS Internet's cost assumptions from *The Paths to 25-50% GenAI ROIC*, **a 35% revenue share above a breakeven level could mean 10%+ upside to FY29 EPS**, and *"a 35% revenue share could mean **>$10bn per GW/yr of 100% margin revenue** to Nvidia."* Mechanism: NVDA backstops neocloud/sovereign credit — *in some cases by being the user of the GPUs itself* if the partner cannot find customers — and in exchange shares in the partner's profit, **booked as 100% gross-margin repeatable revenue**.
- **BofA's framing is the cleanest one-liner on the structure: "NVDA UNDERWRITES THE VALUE, NOT THE LOAN"** — *"the burden sits with the consortium, not NVDA's balance sheet. This appears to be a **pivot away from vendor-financing** … that drew circularity fire."* And on why it matters: *"**Funding, not demand, has been the bottleneck** — every hyperscaler complains of being supply-constrained. A **$500bn pool (2.5x Google's network)** lets **non-investment-grade buyers — labs, neoclouds, sovereigns — secure GPUs, power and data centers at attractive rates**, de-risking offtake and supporting our **$1.7tn CY30 AI systems TAM** path."* Reiterates **Buy, Top Pick, PO $320**; next catalyst **Aug 26 earnings** (BofA / Vivek Arya via Brian Fenske, 2026-08-11).
- **Moore's preferred structure — and it is a live thing to watch per deal:** *"we would prefer a backstop which involves **GPU usage rather than pure credit backing**. The reason is that we know NVIDIA wants to rent those GPUs for its own development in areas such as open source modelling, and there really isn't as much cost to NVIDIA using inexpensive neocloud GPUs at a below-market backstop price as there would be to a straight credit guarantee. But in that context, **judging 25%, and passivity, will be assessed one deal at a time**."* ➜ **This is the falsifiable test for every subsequent platform deal: is the 25% a usage backstop or a credit guarantee?**
- **⚠️ The counterpoints Moore concedes:** NVDA *"will still take on some credit risk — which we knew already — and we could see **more leverage in the overall ecosystem**"*; **$500bn is nominal potential, not committed capital** — *"there's no guarantee that these funds are deployed"*; and the deeper debate is unchanged — *"because of front-loaded investment, **some of the major hyperscalers are now cash flow neutral or negative**… the NVIDIA view… is that this investment is not enough, given token growth of 10x or so, so we need sovereigns and neoclouds to take up that slack. **Not everyone in the investor base agrees, to say the least.**"*
- **🔴⚠️ THE CREDIT MARKET IS THE DISSENTING VOICE, AND IT IS THE ONE DATAPOINT ON THIS PAGE THAT WENT THE WRONG WAY: NVDA's CDS widened +5bps to 77bps against CDX IG at 52bps** on the announcement (MS TMT desk, 2026-08-11), and the WSJ notes debt investors now demand *"~0.40 points over Treasuries"* to lend to NVIDIA itself (via JPM / Joshua Meyers, 2026-08-11). **Also: BofA Credit downgraded [[AVGO]] to Marketweight from Overweight the same day, arguing XPV financing creates "more complicated spread and residual-value risk"** — i.e. the credit desks are pricing the residual-value underwriting as a real liability even where the equity desks are not (TMTB EOD Wrap, 2026-08-11).
- **Jefferies' balanced read on why the tape was negative:** the -3% move stemmed from *"concerns that the AI bubble and 'circular financing' narratives are being further enforced (despite Jensen's post on X directly refuting this)"*, *"the increasing reliance of the AI capex cycle on **debt/leverage, private credit markets, and creative financing** — we have neoclouds using GPUs as collateral already, **is datacenter securitization next?**"*, and *"the scale of financing now required, which is a **step-up vs NVDA's $250bn 'backstop' for OAI**."* The positives: another move to **lock customers into the ecosystem** and *"the clear demand from private capital to fund this AI infra buildout, which helps ease any concerns for funding to be a potential constraint"* (Jefferies / Rankie Wong, 2026-08-11).
- **The partners' own framing (Larry Fink on CNBC, relayed by Jefferies / Conor O'Mara, 2026-08-10 PM):** BlackRock *"have raised some of the capital for this but will be raising more"*; **each GW costs $50–60bn**; **the US alone will need over 70GW**; *"over time this will require **trillions of dollars** of investment, **making compute an asset class**"*; and the analogy — *"the financing of datacentres reminds Larry Fink of **mortgage-backed securities in the 70s**… this is the next future for financial engineering."* ⚠️ Jefferies' financials specialist adds the caveat that matters: *"everyone agrees this $500B **does not represent the equity capital investment** — unclear how much leverage though."* The 6 partners all rallied (APO +6%, BX +4%).
- **⚠️ The bear intellectual case, and it is the most serious one written (Ben Thompson, "Nvidia's Risky Business", Stratechery, 2026-08-11):** NVDA is *"quietly reshaping the AI funding landscape through these third-party capital partnerships, effectively **turning GPU-powered data centers into an institutional infrastructure asset class**."* The catch: *"by **backstopping residual values and drawing on insurance floats and pension capital**, Nvidia is **spreading risk far beyond the balance sheets of hyperscalers**, echoing the **railroad bond mania of the 1870s that ended in the Panic of 1873**."* With frontier labs reducing CUDA dependence, [[GOOG]] pivoting to TPU scale, and **rising spreads / collapsing cover ratios** in debt markets, the question is *"whether AI revenues will materialize before the novel funding mechanisms unravel"* (summary per JPM / Joshua Meyers, 2026-08-11; article forwarded by Daniel Grozdea, 2026-08-11).
- **Who the money actually goes to — the read-through that moved neoclouds:** *"$500 billion will likely go **mainly to neoclouds/OpenAI/Anthropic/SpaceX and NOT the top three hyperscalers** (Amazon, Microsoft, Google). Jensen just figured out a way to **rapidly level up the smaller guys against the hyperscalers with their ASICs**"* (@firstadopter / Tae Kim, 2026-08-11, 285K views). [[NBIS]] +5–6%, [[CRWV]] and the neocloud complex outperformed.

**🆕 2026-08-11 — GS Q2 FY27 PREVIEW: Buy, PT $285, and the house is 6%/19% above the Street on CY26/CY27 (GS / James Schneider, 2026-08-11).** Investor focus expected on **(1) $500bn platform details, (2) the shape of the Rubin ramp in 2H, (3) forward gross-margin trends, (4) potential upside from agentic AI to CPUs.** *"We expect a **solid quarter with meaningful upside to guidance** supported by tight GPU supply/demand trends, but think **the bar for the stock is elevated given its +12% move in two weeks**."* Trades at **14.4x GS CY27E EPS**, a wide discount to their fair value; the three things needed to re-rate: *"(1) improving profitability metrics at hyperscalers that support sustained spending growth; (2) **measured capital outlays in support of customer financing platforms**; (3) reiteration of strong capital returns (buybacks and dividends)."* ➜ **Note (2): GS is explicitly treating the financing platform as a potential *negative* if NVDA's own outlay creeps up — the mirror image of the bull case.**

**🆕 2026-08-10 (PM) — THE $500BN FINANCING PLATFORM IS NOW OFFICIAL, AND IT IS THE STRUCTURAL ANSWER TO THE CIRCULARITY BEAR.** NVDA formally announced partnerships with **Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR** to establish **AI compute infrastructure financing platforms to mobilize over $500 billion of third-party capital** (NVIDIA Newsroom press release, 2026-08-10 17:12; first reported by the FT mid-day Monday). Company framing: demand for AI infrastructure *"continues to accelerate"*, **"NVIDIA compute is an investable asset"**, and NVDA *"will work with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to create dedicated pools of capital at significant scale at attractive rates for NVIDIA customers."* **⚠️ SIZE IT BEFORE BELIEVING IT — the conta, on this page's own $/GW anchor:** at MS's **$39bn all-in capex/GW** (Nowak/Byrd/Wood, 2026-07-27, logged below — $23bn IT on a 5-yr life + $16bn non-IT on a 15-yr life) **$500bn ≈ 12.8 GW**; at the ledger's ~**$50bn/GW** NVDA-GPU-infra mark **≈10.0 GW**; if it funds only the compute leg (~$23bn/GW) **≈21.7 GW**. Against **14-16 facility-GW built in 2026** (Jefferies satellite tracking, 50% haircut) the *entire* pool is **on the order of ONE YEAR of the global buildout — spread over an unstated number of years — and ~9-10% of the cumulative 2026-30 program** (106 GW × ~$50bn ≈ $5.3T; JPM's 138 GW-through-2030 gives the same answer). ⚠️ **Directional, not precise — three unresolved forks:** (a) the $/GW basis swings the answer **2.2x**; (b) if "$500bn of third-party capital" is *fund equity* that then gets levered at infra/ABS LTVs, purchasing power is 2-3x higher; (c) MS's GW is **IT-load**, Jefferies's is **facility** (~1.25x PUE gap) — do not merge them (`ai-dc-power-gw` in [assumptions.md](_meta/assumptions.md)). **Net: a large SLICE of the buildout's financing, not a step-change in its size — and capital was never the binding constraint (MS · Byrd: 38 GW US shortfall through 2028, up to 122 GW through 2030).**
- **Why it matters mechanically (Vital Knowledge / Adam Crisafulli, 2026-08-10):** *"AI chip firms are no longer simply competing on technical specifications… Increasingly, capital is a critical piece of the value proposition as firms contemplate whether to pick Nvidia, AMD, TPU, or someone else."* Crisafulli puts **GOOG/AVGO "running in second place"** on the financing dimension.
- **Bull framing:** the pool *"will act as a major tailwind for demand **without filling up Nvidia's balance sheet**, a win/win."* This is the key structural difference vs the Lancium equity stake and the OpenAI backstop — third-party capital, not NVDA capital.
- **⚠ Bear framing, same source:** *"the company is getting very aggressive in offering all sorts of financial support to customers to ensure demand for its chips stays strong… the AI industry in aggregate continues to have an extreme paucity of cash flow, and capital markets are being forced to plug the gap, but **investors can't absorb an endless supply of debt and equity in perpetuity**."*
- **⚠ Not disclosed and worth chasing:** the split of the $500bn by partner, the tenor, the pricing (*"attractive rates"* is unquantified), and whether NVDA carries any first-loss. The Information's 07-27 precedent on the SK announcement applies — *"NVDA will not say which company is putting up how much"* — so treat the headline number as **capacity to mobilize, not committed capital**, until terms are published. Cross-ref [SPCX.md](SPCX.md), [OPENAI.md](OPENAI.md), [themes/ai-datacenter-power.md](themes/ai-datacenter-power.md).

**🆕 2026-08-10 (PM) — Rubin Ultra HBM: the answer may be BOTH, not either (Morgan Stanley / Charlie Chan · Daniel Yen · Daisy Dai, 2026-08-10).** MS Asia checks re-open the de-spec question the 08-07 UBS note appeared to close: *"we think Nvidia's **Rubin Ultra will feature SEVERAL SKUs**, with the **high-end version adopting HBM4e 8-Hi** and **lower-end versions using HBM4 12-Hi or 8-Hi**"* — i.e. a **tiered spec** driven by (1) HBM capacity shortages, (2) cost pressures, (3) workload-specific memory-capacity requirements. **Final decision before end-3Q26.**
- **The performance cost is workload-specific, not uniform:** *"HBM de-specification will have a **more meaningful impact on DECODING than PRE-FILL workloads**, particularly for long-context-window LLMs."* This is the first attempt on this page to say *where* the de-spec actually bites.
- **Bits offset restated:** *"reducing memory content per chip may increase overall chip shipments, boosting volume-driven suppliers"* — consistent with UBS's 25.1bn Gb / 12.6mn-unit revision. MS adds a warning for the ASIC pages: *"we do not rule out major ASIC projects adopting different HBM configurations for similar reasons."*
- **🔴 Kyber and CPO — no timeline, and Oberon carries Rubin Ultra:** *"given ongoing **PCB and thermal challenges**, first-generation Rubin Ultra server racks will **likely continue to use the Oberon solution for NVL72** while adopting **CPO/NPO technologies to enable NVL576-scale deployments**."* MS remains *"optimistic about Nvidia's adoption of CPO as a key differentiator in scale-up performance versus China's supernode architectures."* This **confirms** the Jefferies/SemiAnalysis Kyber-slip call already on this page and puts the CPO leg on the NVL576 timeline, not NVL72. Cross-ref [MU.md](MU.md), [themes/hbm-memory.md](themes/hbm-memory.md), [themes/optical-cpo.md](themes/optical-cpo.md).

**🆕 2026-08-10 — MS July rack tracker: CY26 NVL72 forecast now 80-85K racks (Morgan Stanley / Howard Kao, 2026-08-10).** Sent to the desk directly. **CY26 full-year NVL72 rack forecast 80-85K**, versus **~29k last year** — i.e. **>100% y/y growth in rack shipments**. It bakes in a recently-raised **Wistron ~3.8K rack-equivalent** revision to **~17.9K**. July by assembler:
| ODM | July revenue | GB200/300 racks (July) | MS FY26 rack forecast |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hon Hai (2317.TW, OW) | NT$946.5bn (+15% m/m, +54% y/y) | **3.6K (+9% m/m)** | ~31.7K (unchanged) |
| Quanta (2382.TW, OW) | NT$366.3bn (-5% m/m, +131% y/y) | **2.2-2.25K (-4% m/m)** | ~18.7K (unchanged) |
| Wistron (3231.TW, OW) | NT$308.2bn (-4% m/m, +61% y/y) | **1,150-1,200 rack-equiv (-6% m/m)** | **~17.9K (raised)** |
Hon Hai's m/m was led by server-related revenue; Quanta's and Wistron's m/m declines are notebook/DT/monitor, not racks. Wiwynn revenue NT$117.7bn (+6% m/m, +39% y/y).
- **Model on disk (saved 2026-08-25):** the note's companion workbook (`Request_NV AI Server Model_081026.xlsx`, from the Kao email) → [NVDA/MS_Kao_NV_AI_Server_Model_2026-08-10.xlsx](../NVDA/MS_Kao_NV_AI_Server_Model_2026-08-10.xlsx) (team copies: `P:\US Equities\Rack B.O.M\` and the P: wiki mirror). 10 sheets: Nvidia Rack Layout · GPU Roadmap · ODM share analysis · GB200-300 monthly Tracker · NVL72 BoM Comparison · per-SKU BoMs (GB200 / GB300 / VR200) — including a **"VR200 BoM (Less Memory)"** variant sheet, i.e. MS's own model carries the de-spec'd memory config as a scenario, consistent with the four de-spec datapoints logged above.

**🆕 2026-08-10 — Nvidia takes a stake in the power, not just the silicon.** NVDA has agreed to invest **$2bn into Lancium** — the power-infrastructure developer behind the **OpenAI/Oracle Stargate campus in Texas** — for **~20%**, and to commit **another $1bn as Lancium secures additional planned power**, which would take it to **~30%** once campuses hit thresholds including grid hookups. The deal values Lancium and its land/power-connection portfolio at **~$10bn enterprise value** including the investment and debt. Backer: **Blackstone**. Stated purpose: **secure multiple gigawatts of pending power rights for Nvidia's chip customers' data projects** as energy becomes the binding constraint (The Information / Ann Davis Vaughan, Valida Pau, Phoebe Liu, 2026-08-07-08; DIGITIMES, 2026-08-10). Vital Knowledge frames it inside the broader capital-structure point — **"the AI industry is demanding capital far above what companies are generating via operating cash flow"** — and notes SemiAnalysis speculation that **Nvidia could provide enormous vendor financing to SpaceX** for Musk's compute build-out (Vital Knowledge / Adam Crisafulli, 2026-08-10). Cross-ref [SPCX.md](SPCX.md), [OPENAI.md](OPENAI.md), [ORCL.md](ORCL.md).

**🆕 The VR300 de-spec is now sized.** UBS checks: first VR300 variant **384GB HBM4/GPU** (8-Hi × 24Gb × 8 × 2 dies), a later version **512GB HBM4E/GPU** around **C3Q27** — *below* UBS's prior 768GB assumption — with the de-spec driven by **persistent HBM supply tightness**; the offset is **more VR300 units in the chain** (UBS / Tim Arcuri, 2026-08-10). Downstream confirmation of the timing slip: **KYEC guided Q3 sales to grow only high-single-digits with GM 37-38% (down q/q) on an Nvidia push-out**, cutting its GM guide to 36-37% from 40%+, and implying **4Q26 revenue +15%+** as **Nvidia and Broadcom ramp in 4Q26, extending into 1Q27** (Jefferies / Conor O'Mara · Sherman Shang, 2026-08-10). Cross-ref [MU.md](MU.md), [AVGO.md](AVGO.md).

**Q1 FY27 (2026-05-20):** Revenue $82B, +85% y/y / +20% q/q — 3rd straight quarter of y/y acceleration, 14th straight q/q gain. Data Center $75B (+92% y/y); compute $60B, networking $15B (nearly tripled y/y). Hyperscale $38B (+12% q/q); ACIE $37B (+31% q/q, AI cloud >3x y/y); sovereign +80% y/y. Non-GAAP GM 75% (flat). Record FCF $49B (vs $35B in Q4). Returned record $20B to holders; dividend raised $0.01→$0.25, new $80B buyback on top of $39B remaining; ~50% of FCF to be returned this year.
- **Guide:** Q2 FY27 revenue **$91B ±2%**, growth led by Data Center. GM mid-70s for FY. **No China DC compute in the outlook** (H200 licenses approved but no revenue recognized).
- **Roadmap:** Vera Rubin production shipments begin **2H, starting Q3 (Oct qtr)**, ramping into Q4/Q1; mgmt expects every cloud/model builder to deploy it. Reiterated **$1T Blackwell+Rubin revenue visibility cal-25 through cal-27**. New **Vera standalone CPU = $200B TAM**, with ~$20B CPU revenue visibility this year (Vivek Arya Q&A: the $20B is standalone). Jensen frames AI infra spend reaching **$3–4T/yr by end of decade**; hyperscale capex >$1T in 2027.
- **Management's own TAM framing — GTC FY26 analyst deck (NVDA GTC Financial Analyst Q&A, 2025-03-19):** the deck lays out the three TAM pillars NVDA now sells against: a **$1T computing inflection point** (accelerated-computing transition), **AI infrastructure for ~$500B enterprise IT** (new compute + networking + storage + software), and **physical AI / robotics framed as a ~$50T industrial-and-robotics** opportunity — the largest, longest-dated leg of the story and the strategic rationale behind the Automotive/physical-AI and Omniverse push. On product, the deck positions **Vera Rubin + NVIDIA Photonics as the "annual rhythm for the world to build out AI infrastructure"** (i.e. management formalizing the one-architecture-per-year cadence), with **Blackwell in full production = "fastest ramp in company history."** On inference economics it claims **Blackwell = 40X Hopper**, and **Blackwell NVL72 + Dynamo = 40X for inference with reasoning models 100X one-shot** — the management-stated efficiency case underpinning the tokens-per-watt / AI-factory-ROI bull argument. Read-through: these are aspirational/strategic TAMs (not bottoms-up models) but anchor how Jensen sizes the runway — the $50T physical-AI figure dwarfs the data-center TAM and is the part the sell-side has yet to underwrite.
- **Rubin power step-up (JPM AI Datacenters & Power, 2025-11-04):** GPU TDP growth accelerating to **50%+** in Rubin vs. the 20-30% historical CAGR; **Rubin Ultra = 4 dies/chip (~5.3kW) vs. Rubin's 2 dies (~2.3kW)**. Rack design power scales DGX B200/B300 ~20kW → **GB200 NVL72 ~198kW → GB300 NVL72 ~288kW → VR200 ~330-444kW → VR Ultra ~1.5MW**, with the 800V HVDC power rack arriving on VR Ultra. Blackwell/Rubin GPUs now ~70-72% of rack system power (vs. 36%/47% for A100/H100). Critically, JPM models NVDA high-end GPU **units declining ~25% in 2028** (6,655k → 4,991k) purely on die-count rising (2→4 dies/chip) — unit prints will understate revenue/compute. A new high-end **CPX** SKU adds TAM from 2027 (assumes 144 CPX/rack, 10-15% attach 2027/28). JPM keeps 2025/26 NVDA GPU shipment forecasts ~unchanged but lifts the GB/VR server mix in 2026-28.
- **Scale-up / networking (MS Scale-up primer):** NVLink delivers ~7.2 Tbit/s per GPU today, doubling to **14.4 Tbit/s per GPU in Rubin** via bi-directional SerDes; in NVL72 (GB200/300) all 72 GPUs are clustered exclusively over NVLink, and **NVLink Fusion** extends it to hybrid custom-ASIC/CPU configs (MS reads this as an NVLink extension, not a true open play). Outside NVDA's stack the scale-up greenfield (UALink, Broadcom's Scale-up Ethernet, PCIe) is where ALAB/AVGO/MRVL compete — i.e. the merchant attack is on the non-NVDA accelerators, not NVLink itself.
- Q4 FY26 (2026-02-25) context: rev $68B (+73%), FY26 DC $194B (+68%), FY26 FCF $97B; ~9 GW Blackwell deployed; SBC now in non-GAAP from Q1 FY27.
- **Vera Rubin timing — Q4, not Q3 (BofA Vivek Arya, NVDA setup call, 2026-05-19):** Arya's plan-of-record read is Rubin ships *to the supply chain* in Q3 (revenue recognized as it shipped Blackwell ahead of end-customer receipt — cf. the ~$11B Blackwell shipped-but-not-received quarter), but the **real big external-customer ramp is late this year into early next year**, i.e. a **Q4 launch with real numbers** (~$0 plan for Q3 public instances). Rubin uses extreme engineering on HBM4 nobody else is running yet; NVDA had ~2-3 designs ready and at least one works well even on HBM4 (10-11 Gbit/s specs). The Hopper→Blackwell jump (8→72 GPU scale-up domain) was far harder; Rubin stays in the NVL72 scale-up domain so the ramp should be cleaner.
- **Rack-power / 800V HVDC arrives on Rubin Ultra, NOT Vera Rubin (AlphaSense 800V expert call, 2026-06-03):** Two ex-Google/Eaton DC-infra experts frame **NVIDIA's Kyber rack (2027/2028) as *the* inflection point for 800V DC** in the data center; Vera Rubin (mid-2027) still ships on a **480V (US) / 415V (EU) power shelf** per NVDA's own documentation. NVDA told them last year the 800V move targets **~7% electricity-efficiency gain** (lab studies: ~78% AC-system efficiency → ~94% with 800V DC) — explicitly so the customer "can take that 7% and buy more chips." Adoption is component-gated (power shelves, DC breakers, solid-state transformers) and safety-gated (arc-flash at 800V/10kA); sidecar power likely bridges first, with an OCP-driven UL spec due before year-end. One large enterprise/hyperscaler-crossover buyer has stated it won't adopt DC until 2032 — i.e. the transition is "evolution, not revolution." Read-through: confirms 800V HVDC content steps up on VR Ultra/Kyber (consistent with JPM's roadmap), and that the marginal rack-power $ accrues 2027+.
- **CPU "$20B" disclosure — back-solving the units (Citi/Jefferies Asia recal, 2026-05-22):** NVDA's standalone-CPU $20B framing implies an implausible unit count at a ~$5-6k ASP (~7-8M units) or AMD-like ASP (~10M units) — the analyst's reconciliation is the number bundles NVLink + the head-node CPU (~3-4M head nodes) + Smart-NIC CPUs + true standalone, not a clean merchant-CPU print. Arm royalty leverage is mostly "companion CPUs" (fixed CPU:GPU ratio in AI servers, ~99% Arm in GB/VR), with the agentic-CPU TAM still largely x86-native software. Read-through: corroborates Arcuri's ~$5B "apples-to-apples chip" haircut on the $20B Vera number; **Google Axion mix at ~60% and AWS Graviton ~60% of general-purpose server mix** were higher than expected (x86 volume headwind).
- **HBM-price / BOM-consignment risk (Redburn "Conor O'Mara Asia Trip Takeaways", 2026-06-23):** NVIDIA HBM pricing goes from **$17-18/GB (2026) → $30-32/GB (2027), a +70-80% step** (pricing for others likely even higher). At that level the **GPU chip + HBM alone reaches ~$4.3M** per rack (~60% of BOM at a 75% NVDA HBM margin; ~$20→ implied chip $55-60K ×72), and the **total memory bill (incl. SOCAMM/LPDDR5/NAND) approaches ~$200B next year**. The live risk: if hyperscalers refuse to let NVDA keep a ~75% margin on a ~40-60% BOM slice, they could push to **consign HBM directly**, which compresses NVDA revenue, ASP and EPS — "the stock that looks cheap isn't so cheap anymore." On NAND, **Kioxia's Super IO (XL Flash, SLC, ultra-low-latency for agentic workloads) has NVIDIA as a partner** (3M units '25 → 10M '26 → 100M '27 target) (Redburn "Conor O'Mara Asia Trip Takeaways", 2026-06-23).
- **NVDA gets the LOWEST HBM price; LPDDR5 the 2027 pinch (StoneX/TrendForce "Memory expert call — Avril", 2026-06-23):** because NVIDIA's HBM volume is the largest and the buyer pool is small, **NVIDIA is expected to receive the lowest HBM price** of any customer (AMD, Broadcom, AWS all priced higher); HBM4 must roughly triple to ~$5/Gb in 2027 (from ~$2.05/Gb) to keep suppliers allocating HBM wafers. Separately, **Low Power DDR5 becomes the single tightest-supply product in 2027** as NVIDIA's Vera / next-gen CPU (SOCAMM) and smartphones compete for it — potential for QoQ price acceleration to resume (StoneX/TrendForce "Memory expert call — Avril", 2026-06-23).
- **HBM roadmap / "most profitable HBM vendor" framing (SemiAnalysis "Scaling the Memory Wall: The Rise and Roadmap of HBM", 2025-08-11):** NVDA commands the "lion's share" of HBM demand through 2027 despite the ASIC rise; **Rubin Ultra pushes per-GPU HBM capacity to 1TB** (roadmap: A100's 80GB HBM2E → 1024GB HBM4E on Rubin Ultra; H100 80GB@3TB/s → GB200 192GB@8TB/s). NVDA (and AMD) are expected to ship custom HBM4 base-die implementations first (2025/26), with other ASIC designers not following until HBM4E (~2027) — a structural lead time advantage baked into the memory supply chain. The GH100 die alone carries 12 HBM controllers on-die; Rubin/MI400-class designs add off-package LPDDR as a second memory tier via the base-die PHY, and Rubin Ultra's oblong single-row-of-SOCs package (vs Blackwell's dual-SOC MCM square grid) doubles usable HBM sites vs Blackwell's 8-site max. The report's framing: "arguably it is Nvidia that is the most profitable HBM vendor in the world" — it captures gross margin on HBM shipped inside its own accelerators, which corroborates (and predates, by ~10 months) the wiki's own 2026-06 Redburn/StoneX HBM-margin-capture debate below. Samsung's HBM3E was qualified specifically for NVDA's H20; NVDA was "well supplied" with HBM3E in 2025, with demand shifting to HBM4 as Rubin ramps (SemiAnalysis, 2025-08-11).
- **Memory shortage forcing DRAM "nerfing" (MS Joe Moore, memory+semicap call, 2026-06-22):** MS flags **NVDA cutting LPDDR5 content roughly in half in the Vera Rubin racks** — read not as bad news but as a tell of how acute the memory shortage is ("everything is being nerfed"); when supply loosens "NVDA's going to double the memory in their racks again." Moore reads **DRAM as the primary bottleneck for AI builds right now, worse than the CPU shortage**, with HBM/most server DRAM for next year already being told to customers as sold out (JPM TMC, 2026-05-22 corroborates). Fast-token economics also a demand tailwind: a 2x-faster token costs ~10-12x more, so low-latency silicon (Groq/Cerebras, which NVDA commercialized via the Groq LPU) is a niche ~10-20% of the market, not a GPU substitute.

NVDA GPU unit shipments modeled **6.2M (2025) → 8.9M (2026E, +39%) → 9.9M (2027E)**; total accelerator units (GPU+ASIC) 10.1M→16.3M→23.3M, with GPUs falling from 68% of units (2025) to 58% (2026E) to 47% (2027E) as ASICs out-ship GPUs (ASIC units +109% y/y in 2026 vs GPU +39%). OpenAI's NVDA deal (≥10 GW, ≥$100B NVDA equity in OAI disbursed per-GW) + first Vera Rubin deployments in 2H26; aggregate OpenAI compute commitments (NVDA+AMD+AVGO) >$1T over 4-5 yrs with 50-60% to compute partners.
- **Per-GW WAFER bill (node split) — NEW 2026-08-25, the physical-units companion to the $/GW cards above.** **Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis)** puts 1 GW of **Vera Rubin** at **55,000 N3 + 6,000 N5 + 170,000 DRAM wafers ≈ 231k 300mm wafers/GW**. **Source: Dylan Patel (SemiAnalysis), in interview — relayed by Felipe, 2026-08-25.** ⚠️ **VINTAGE, not attribution, is the open item: Patel dates the figures to an interview “a few months” earlier, so carry them as ~2Q26 vintage rather than a fresh mark — which matters because the SOCAMM spec has been halved since (see the sensitivity below).** **House reconciliation (Capstone, 2026-08-25):** the denominator is **~4,440-4,545 racks/GW** — VR200 draw ~220-225kW per rack, where TrendForce (~225kW, 06-28 row below) and Bernstein (220kW compute-TDP) agree independently; ⚠️ JPM's **330-444kW 'rack design power'** (2025-11-04 bullet above) is nameplate, and **Redburn's 3,130 racks/GW is a FACILITY-GW figure** (PUE 1.15 → 870MW IT → 90% to GPU racks → 250kW/rack ⇒ 225,391 GPUs/GW) — three different denominators, never interchangeable. On the ~4,500-rack basis the **DRAM leg is confirmed** (72 × 288GB HBM4 + 36 × 768GB SOCAMM per rack ⇒ 141-205k DRAM wafers/GW; NVDA's official *75TB of fast memory per NVL144* is the pre-cut 20.7TB HBM + 54TB SOCAMM), while the **logic leg is ~2x a die-area bottom-up of the NVL144 BOM** (~25-30k N3/GW vs the quoted 61k; ⚠️ **CPX cannot close the gap at JPM's 144 CPX/rack × 10-15% attach**). Ledger: [`wafers-per-gw`](_meta/assumptions.md); worked through on [[TSM]] and [themes/hbm-memory](themes/hbm-memory.md).

NVDA has "maintained share very handsomely" the last few years and likely *gained* share ex-Anthropic in 2025-26; panel skeptical AMD lands the full ~6 of 27 GW (~30% of openly-committed GW) it's on paper for. Gavin Baker: ">200B inference revenue exiting 2026," MS 2027 hyperscale capex chart lifted $950B→$1.1T (panel thinks ~$1.5T incl. SpaceX/neoclouds).

Despite the beat, **the stock fell ~3% over the two days after the print** — Barron's frames Huang's own line, "we should be growing faster than hyperscale capex," as "a key point of concern for investors" given hyperscaler growth (+115%) is now outpacing the smaller-customer bucket (+74%) (Barron's/Adam Levine, 2026-05-25).

Rubin GPU ramp was slower in Q2'26 on redesigns but UBS still expects Rubin to reach **2.1mn units for 2026** with a steep 2H'26 pickup (UBS · Sunny Lin, 2026-07-01). Because **CPO NVSwitch won't be available until Feynman**, NVDA currently has **no proven solution to expand the scale-up world size for Rubin Ultra** — leaving an opening for **AMD MI500X** and **GOOGL TPUv8i 'Broadfly'** to gain scale-up advantages. This is a genuine competitive-risk nuance (bear-ish for the scale-up roadmap), sharpening the earlier Jefferies (06-22) "Kyber slips to ≥2028, Rubin Ultra stays on Oberon/NVL72" read with the specific manufacturability cause and the NVL576/NVL72x2 fallout. (SemiAnalysis, via CNBC & MS TMT · 2026-07-06)
- **NVDA as the AI-debt "central bank" (SemiAnalysis, via Vital Knowledge, 2026-07-06):** SemiAnalysis frames the AI debt-financing market as set to **exceed $7T by 2029** — which would be the 2nd-largest ABS sector after mortgages — with NVDA acting as the "central bank" of this financing by providing **revenue guarantees to neoclouds** so that data centers without a hyperscaler anchor customer can still be built. Extends the 07-02 The-Information "NVDA backstops customers' GPUs for a cut of cloud revenue" datapoint (below) into a systemic-scale framing. Bull: de-risks the buildout and locks in the ecosystem; bear: another sign the cycle increasingly depends on NVDA-provided financial engineering (circular-financing critique). (SemiAnalysis, via Vital Knowledge · 2026-07-06)
- **GPU backstop program — mechanics + read from the primary note (SemiAnalysis "Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop Unleashes the AI Project Trinity", 2026-07-06):** the full paid note quantifies the backstop the 07-06 Vital-Knowledge/07-02 The-Information items summarized. In the program NVDA gives Neoclouds a **take-or-pay commitment — a minimum-revenue guarantee on the underlying GPU capacity** — and in exchange **shares in a portion of the Neocloud's revenue earned above the backstop level**; the Neocloud stays free to rent to any customer at any tenor, and **the intent is the backstop is never actually invoked** (SemiAnalysis "Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop...", 2026-07-06). Objectives: (1) broaden compute access beyond a few hyperscalers/large AI labs and enable **shorter-than-5yr rental tenors**, (2) buy lenders time up the risk-pricing learning curve, (3) grow Neoclouds into bankable, diversified-client-book platforms that can also press custom-silicon against NVDA's systems. Because lenders lean on NVDA's **AA/Aa2 investment-grade** balance sheet behind the backstop, it unlocks all three legs of the **"AI Project Trinity" (Capital, Offtake, Datacenter)** for Neoclouds that otherwise can't raise debt outside a 5yr IG-hyperscaler-backstopped template. NVDA is also **directly leasing datacenter capacity and subleasing to Neoclouds** to close the hardest (Datacenter) leg. Crucially for the demand debate, SemiAnalysis reiterates the market is **still materially below its supply-chain-tracked Accelerator Model on NVDA's 2H 2026 GPU shipment volumes and revenue** — 3 years into the buildout. Macro backdrop from the same note: **>$7T AI debt outstanding by 2029** (2nd-largest ABS market after US MBS ~$13T), annual AI capex **>$2T in 2028**, and cumulative AI capex 2024–2029 **~$11.1T**, with Oracle→Meta→Google increasingly funding buildouts with debt. Bull: NVDA grows the pie and takes a bigger, recurring, near-pure-margin slice; bear: sharpens the circular-financing critique. (SemiAnalysis "Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop...", 2026-07-06)
- **Backstop economics — the modelled numbers (SemiAnalysis "Nvidia GPU Debt Backstop Unleashes the AI Project Trinity: Capital, Offtake and Datacenters", 2026-07-06; net-new quantification added on the 2026-07-24 dedup pass off the primary SemiAnalysis email copy):** the arithmetic behind the mechanics bullet above, none of which was on the page. **Term is typically six years**, over which Nvidia stands ready to purchase compute at pre-agreed price levels that vary through the period; above the floor Nvidia takes a **revenue share modelled at 40–60%, working out to a ~18–20% take rate on average over the life of the deal**. The illustrative curve SemiAnalysis presents (deliberately at the *low end* of the backstop range) averages **$2.36/hr over the six years, starting at $3.68/hr in year 1** against an assumed $6.75/hr year-1 customer rental price. **Accounting — the part that matters for the balance-sheet debate:** these deals sit on a **cloud service agreement line, "a contingent guarantee rather than a funded asset — making this an off-balance-sheet line unless triggered"**; the revenue share itself is **near-pure margin and recurring**. **Modelled trajectory:** cloud service agreements reach **$77.5B by end-F1/27 and up to $175.3B by end-F1/29**, i.e. **~$5.9B of contingent guarantee added per 100MW backstopped**, driving **incremental NVDA revenue of $1.8B in F1/27 rising to $13.9B in F1/29**, on **932MW under the program in F1/27 (of which 432MW already announced — 360MW Firmus + 72MW SharonAI), plus 1,000MW in F1/28 and 1,500MW in F1/29**. **Calibration (why lenders bite and operators don't get lazy):** a neocloud earns **25.4% IRR on a 1-year rental book under the backstop vs 40.7% unbackstopped**, and **~zero or slightly negative if the backstop is actually triggered** — sized so banks clear a **DSCR of at least 1.3x in the backstop-activated scenario, typically a 70–80% LTV**. Strategically the note frames Nvidia's buyers as **four concentric pools** (all buyers → neoclouds → certified NCPs → NCPs with a backstop), each narrower and each worth more to Nvidia: at the innermost pool "the one-time hardware sale becomes a recurring, near-pure-margin incremental revenue stream, and Nvidia gains a partial claim on the downstream rental economics it used to give away at the point of sale" — the "**Nvidia as the Central Bank of AI**" framing already summarized on this page, now with the mechanism attached. **Announced deals (all APAC so far):** **SharonAI** — 72MW AI factory in Australia, scaling to as many as **40,000 GB300s** under a six-year backstop, **$4.88B disclosed backstop value = ~$2.33/hr/GPU implied floor**, footprint growing to 132MW with 102MW contracted and >55,000 Nvidia GPUs by mid-2027; **Firmus** — **360MW in Batam, Indonesia** (announced 2026-06-29, likely a DayOne facility), guiding **$25–30B of customer revenue over six years**. Scale check on how new this all is: Nvidia's program **started at an $860M lease guarantee in October 2025 (in exchange for warrants) and had risen to $3.5B by January 2026** (SemiAnalysis "Can AMD break the CUDA Moat?", 2026-07-24) — versus the $77.5B/$175.3B trajectory modelled above. **The bear side SemiAnalysis itself keeps:** three named obstacles to the market ever reaching ~$7.1T — (1) "**Hyperscaler balance sheets will not be able to backstop trillions of dollars' worth of compute**," and outside a 5-yr hyperscale-backstopped template "the appetite to lend drops off almost entirely"; (2) **lenders are still on the learning curve** — most banks have "a nascent understanding of AI Cluster total cost of ownership… and still hide behind the shield of an investment grade offtake or backstop"; (3) **no pricing/risk tooling** — GPU rental transactions are bilateral and unpublished and "there is no active derivatives market to provide a pricing signal or a good reference for GPU residual value." Also from the same note: **neocloud colocation leases carry a 3–5% higher yield-on-cost** than hyperscale/IG deals, and inference providers refuse tenors beyond 1yr, with some neoclouds extracting **prepays up to 100% of contract value** (a theoretically infinite IRR). [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_06_ENC_Nvidia_GPU_Debt_Backstop_Unleashes_the_AI_Project_Trinity_Capital_Offtake_and_Datacenters_email.html)
- **Rubin vs MI455X — the microarchitecture and co-design case, quantified (SemiAnalysis "Can AMD break the CUDA Moat? AMD Advancing AI 2026", 2026-07-24):** SemiAnalysis's AMD Advancing-AI teardown is, read from the NVDA side, the most specific competitive scorecard on the page. **Compute:** MI455X marks **20 PF dense FP8 vs Rubin's 17,500 TFLOPs (17.5 PF)** — a mild AMD lead, but on far more silicon (3,470 mm² of logic per package, N2 vs everyone else's N3) and **"down to AMD's deficit to Nvidia in GPU microarchitecture design"**: MI455X **lacks the 3-bit LUT tensor cores Rubin's SM107 has**, which reduce the relative HBM-bandwidth requirement, and CDNA 5 "barely scales MMA shapes" where Nvidia has scaled them aggressively every generation. **Memory — a deliberate Nvidia gambit:** MI455X carries 12 HBM4 stacks / 432GB / **23.3 TB/s** vs Rubin's 8 stacks / 288GB / **22 TB/s**; Nvidia closed a 50%-wider-bus deficit by **raising targeted HBM4 pin speed to 10.7 Gbps — well above the original JEDEC HBM4 spec and 40% faster than AMD's 7.6 Gbps** — "precisely driven by the need to make up for the memory bandwidth deficit to AMD MI455X." Cost of that gambit: **memory suppliers had to rework their HBM4**, it **pushed out upstream Rubin output (now resolved)**, and **Nvidia "will be forced to use a much higher quality bin than AMD"** — the specific mechanism behind the HBM4-pricing/GM thread already on this page. Verdict: **"despite the delays, Vera Rubin will still be the first to deliver tokens at scale compared to MI455 Helios."** **Rack co-design — the clearest NVDA moat datapoint:** AMD's Helios is on a **slow rack production ramp specifically "due to the lack of a cableless design compared to Rubin Oberon rack"**; on scale-up, each Broadcom Tomahawk-6 switch in Helios uses only **432 of its 512 200G lanes** (over-provisioning forced by using a merchant switch), whereas "**Nvidia designed the 28.8T NVSwitch to match the needs of a 72 GPU rack**" and it divides evenly with no waste. **Power is the outlier in NVDA's favour:** MI455X draws **~240kW server / ~257kW all-in per rack vs GB300 NVL72's ~142kW / ~159kW** — and while MI455X screens competitive on TCO per *marketed* dense-FP8 PFLOP, SemiAnalysis flags AMD "has historically overstated TFLOPs" and suspects low MFU, so effective training throughput is likely lower. **The harsher note for NVDA, kept as written:** AMD gaining share "doesn't mean NVIDIA will do poorly — the pie is getting massive," but **"Jensen will need to cut bureaucracy & layers of different required internal stakeholder approvals, for even the simplest of tasks, at NVIDIA to move faster and defend their lead."** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_24_ENC_Can_AMD_break_the_CUDA_Moat_AMD_Advancing_AI_2026_email.html)
- **Meta's whole GB200 fleet was the off-standard Ariel SKU; GB300 goes back to standard — a demand-mix positive (SemiAnalysis "Meta's Infrastructure Team Needs A Culture Reset", 2026-07-21):** Meta's custom **Ariel NVL36x2** depopulated one GPU on the standard Bianca board to run **1 B200 per Grace** (vs the standard 2:1) for RecSys embeddings, at **14% higher TCO than a standard GB200 NVL72** and worse $/FLOP and $/HBM — "this decision cost Meta billions of dollars." **Meta's entire GB200 fleet was Ariel.** The 36x2 configuration was **dropped industry-wide for GB300 and Meta is now buying the standard configuration** — i.e. a large customer normalizing back onto NVDA's reference rack. Same note: Meta's software stack still depends on **Nvidia's version of RoCE**, so Meta was never realistically switching NIC vendors, and **GB300 deployments run Nvidia NICs** (and NSF) — a check on the merchant-networking-displacement bear. [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2026_07_21_ENC_Metas_Infrastructure_Team_Needs_A_Culture_Reset_email.html)
