NVDA framed growth around the **new 3-segment structure**: (1) **AI labs ~20% of total demand** — one of the more prominent frontier models was built mostly on an ASIC so NVDA had minimal exposure, but NVDA share there has since risen to **~50%**, while other frontier models remain mostly on NVDA; (2) **traditional hyperscalers ~half of revenue** — increasingly capped by land/space & power, but SAM expanding via networking and now CPU (repeated the **$20B CPU target this year**, with **~half of that outside the head node** = a substantial standalone-CPU-rack presence with **Vera in 2H**, purpose-built for single-threaded workloads with a large die, smaller core counts, AI-optimized memory); (3) **"AI clouds, industrial & enterprise" ~half of DC revenue** — sovereign/reshoring-driven, minimal competition, fragmented but large-scale (retail/finance/biotech, regional AI capacity). MS view: **both NVDA & AVGO AI businesses grow 80%+ next year and are supply-constrained → no dramatic ASIC-vs-GPU share shift**; contacts substantiate that **the lowest cost per token is frequently from NVDA** (cheaper silicon ≠ better token economics), and NVDA's compute share climbed 2024→2026. **Product roadmap tracking:** a strong Vera Rubin cycle drives the next 12mo; on the "Rubin Ultra slips to 2028" stories the company said that is **not true — Rubin Ultra ships next year**, but acknowledged form-factor changes as the **Kyber rack is being replaced by a "better solution"** potentially supporting a **larger single-rack scale-up domain** (presented as a positive); **800V + optical scale-up between racks remain on schedule**. **Memory shortage** looks to last several years — NVDA cut **LPDDR5 content per rack in half** to meet rack demand; compute/networking/memory are inter-related and NVDA can use two to optimize a shortage of the third; management highlighted **Groq SRAM** ("used to be much more expensive than DRAM"). **Capital return / value pitch:** with **50%+ of cash flow moving to cash return starting now**, MS argues NVDA is "a very clear value name amid large caps" — this NDR was explicitly designed to **broaden the investor base to value-centric investors** (closing the value gap vs. compute-semis peers). Also flagged the new **neocloud business model** (co-investment + credit assurance + revenue-sharing) — investors have focused on the credit-backstop downside, but the **revenue-sharing** upside could make NVDA a **partial owner of a large network of GPU clouds** — and **"nemotron"** open-model development that lets enterprise customers own the full stack for app-specific AI (e.g. circuit design). Traditional cloud (4-5 US hyperscalers) ≈ half of revenue, holding strong share vs the "ASIC thread and AMD thread" while expanding TAM into networking + CPUs; the third bucket (AI cloud / enterprise / sovereign-reshoring) has "no competition, no ASICs coming in." **ASIC confidence — NVDA at ~85% revenue share, "a level they can sustain"** (Moore: management much more confident than the market perceives; the Computex chart argues NVDA has the highest tokens-per-GW, fastest bring-up, longest meantime-between-failure and **longest asset life** vs a single-purpose ASIC — "the stock market gives ASICs too much credit"). **Vera CPU $20B decomposed:** ~$10B head-node + ~$2B other AI-rack content (storage etc.) + **~$8B standalone server** (mostly 2H since Vera only shipped mid-year, so the run-rate "moves significantly higher"); trims the *peak* earnings power for memory makers vs the crisis feel of 3 months ago but is durable — Jensen: **"your Micron stock will be fine."** On GM, mgmt reiterates mid-70s around this product cycle (HBM4 re-pricing ~a year out the risk), but **MS models NVDA gross margin down to 73% next year** (deliberately conservative). **Kyber — development STOPPED:** Ruben Ultra "very much on track for next year," but **Kyber is giving way to a different technology — NVDA has stopped Kyber development and is "doing something better,"** a superior scale-up domain read as **>576 die/rack** (die-per-package also shifting 4→2); On packaging mix, Nvidia's **flagship GPUs use TSMC's CoWoS-L**; **some products use CoWoS-S/R**, which — given TSMC's CoWoS-S/R capacity constraint — are increasingly outsourced to OSATs (**ASE, Amkor**); the transcript names "Nvidia's V100" as a CoWoS-S example (attributed as stated). - **🆕 Feynman is the lead CoPoS product — the packaging platform behind the 2028+ roadmap, sized (UBS · Sunny Lin / Randy Abrams / Timothy Arcuri et al, "Can Intel challenge TSMC's advanced packaging leadership? — Intel's EMIB-T vs TSMC's CoPoS", 2026-07-27).** UBS's advanced-packaging deep-dive is a TSMC/Intel note, but it puts NVDA first in line on the next packaging generation. **The core call: "TSMC will likely start CoPoS ramp with 310x310mm² panels for the first generation, with mass production targeted for 2028. We believe Nvidia's Feynman may be the first CoPoS client in H228-2029, followed by AMD and ASICs in 2029-30"** — and UBS's whole TSMC share model is built "assuming CoPoS enters mass production for Nvidia in 2028, and for others in 2029-30." So Nvidia is both the anchor tenant and the timing gate for the CoPoS transition; TSMC could later enhance scalability by migrating to larger 510x515mm² panels. **What CoPoS buys the roadmap:** UBS frames it as "a full-generation upgrade to CoWoS rather than merely a packaging form-factor transition" — stronger package-level performance via tighter interconnect and better signal integrity, plus "broader integration options such as embedded capacitors, **3D stacking** and eventually **co-packaged optics (CPO)**" — i.e. the packaging substrate for exactly the CPO-NVSwitch-at-Feynman thread already on this page. **The near-term CoWoS ceiling, quantified from the same note:** separately from CoPoS, "TSMC has added **14x-reticle CoWoS** to its roadmap, with support for around **10 large compute dies and 20 HBM stacks**… slated for production in **2028**, with the potential to scale beyond 14x reticle in 2029" (_this is the 14x-reticle **CoWoS** spec, not a CoPoS spec — attribute precisely_); UBS notes "scaling CoWoS beyond 10x reticle remains challenging" and that CoPoS is the better answer for larger packages. On the competing platform, UBS thinks **Intel's EMIB-T could hold an edge on ultra-large packages (12-14x reticle or larger)** because it avoids an ultra-large interposer — relevant to whichever path Feynman-class packages ultimately take. **Why the alternatives exist at all — the supply backdrop:** "due to **persistent CoWoS capacity constraints at TSMC in recent years**, other advanced packaging solutions from competing foundries and OSATs are gaining traction," with EMIB-T "emerging as a competitive alternative given TSMC's supply constraints and growing interest in supply-chain diversification" among Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom. That is the same CoWoS-allocation squeeze the page tracks via Nomura (06-30) and Jefferies (07-17), now stated as the structural driver of platform fragmentation. **Substrate supply — the NVDA BOM read:** UBS puts **Ibiden's current market share of ABF substrate in NVIDIA Blackwell / Blackwell Ultra GPUs at 70-80%**, on a track record including CoWoS-L and demonstrated warpage control; it expects Ibiden to hold that position through the CoPoS transition because "reliability and manufacturing track record are likely to outweigh cost considerations, **given ABF package costs represent only a small portion of the overall bill of materials for GPU/HBM**" — i.e. a genuine single-supplier concentration, but on a low-value BOM line, and UBS expects customers to pursue multi-sourcing anyway given the anticipated shortage of high-end ABF substrates. Among Taiwan substrate makers UBS names **Unimicron** a key CoPoS beneficiary (with Nan Ya PCB expanding too); Unimicron is also a potential second source on Intel's EMIB-T if volumes surprise. **Platform-level TAM:** advanced-packaging industry revenue **US$19.0bn (2026E) → US$36.3bn ('27) → US$58.1bn ('28) → US$87.1bn ('29) → US$122.0bn (2030E), a 59% CAGR**, with TSMC modeled at 84%/82% share in 2026-27 falling to **65-70% by 2030** in UBS's stress test (62% in the lower case) as Intel's EMIB-T takes 13-18%. ⚠️ **No NVDA rating or price target in this note** — UBS's disclosure page lists **NVIDIA Corp at US$208.76 (23 Jul 2026)** as an additional-price reference only; the page's existing PT cluster (MS $288, BofA $350, Barclays $275, DB $255, UBS house $280-285/Arcuri) is untouched. (UBS · Sunny Lin / Randy Abrams / Timothy Arcuri et al, 2026-07-27) [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/UBS_on_adv_packaging.html)

## Debate / thesis
**🗄️ ARCHIVE BACKFILL — DAMNANG (Substack), 2026-07-07 / 2026-04-25 / 2026-03-22.** ⚠️ **INDEPENDENT AUTHOR, NOT A BROKER — no rating, no PT, no model.** Same author already cited on this page (damnang2.substack.com; also publishes as "The Optical Edge"); launched 2026-03-15, ~9k subscribers, paid. These entries are 1-4 months old and are filed as historical context only; nothing here supersedes any current number, rating or thesis on this page.**
- **🆕 The most useful archive item is a RE-READ OF SEMIANALYSIS'S OWN KYBER-DELAY CLAIM, and this page has been carrying that claim since 07-06** (**DAMNANG (Substack)** — "A Complete Guide to NVIDIA's Racks, and Then SemiAnalysis", **2026-07-07**; ⚠️ independent author, NOT a broker). DAMNANG summarises SemiAnalysis's four claims — Kyber NVL144 slipping to 2028 on midplane manufacturability; NVL576 *"delayed or limited to small volumes"*; NVL72×2 cancelled after cloud-provider pushback; and the four-die Rubin Ultra cancelled, leaving only two-die — then attacks the FRAMING rather than the facts: *"The problem with these claims is not that every sentence is false. Each sentence is written so it can be walked back no matter how things turn out, while the overall framing makes it read as if the entire Rubin Ultra generation is wobbling."* 🔴 **His sharpest point is arithmetic and this page should hold it: Kyber's official schedule is 2H 2027, so a genuine ">12-month delay" would put it in LATE 2028, not early 2028 — the piece conflates "slipping into early 2028" with "slipping by more than 12 months."** On NVL72×2 he notes it *"was never officially announced by NVIDIA. It existed only in supply chain reporting as an internal alternative under consideration"*, so *"cancellation of a product that was never announced has no reference point against which to check it."* On the midplane he argues the design is itself a yield defence — *"three 26-layer boards into a 78-layer stack nearly one square meter in area, with trace spacing at or below 25 micrometers"*, holding electrical characteristics *"within a 5 percent tolerance"*, testable as known-good sub-boards — and that a passive board at 50% yield *"doubles the cost of the board"* without breaking the economics of a multi-million-dollar rack. He also cites Jensen at CES 2026 that the midplane *"cut tray assembly time from two hours to five minutes"*, and NVIDIA's one-line rebuttal, *"Our roadmap is intact."* **Rack power ladder from the same piece: ~40kW (Hopper) → 120–130kW (Blackwell) → 190–230kW (Rubin) → *"the 600 kW class"* for Kyber; Oberon cabinet 0.6m × 1.1m × 2.2m at 1.4 tons; VR200 NVL72 = 72 GPU packages + 36 Vera CPUs; Kyber stands trays vertically for 144 packages per rack.** ⚠️ **This is one independent author's reading, not evidence — and it is 7 weeks old. It does NOT overturn the Kyber-delay entries under `## Risks`, which remain the page's working assumption. It is filed because it is the only source on this page that checks SemiAnalysis's arithmetic against NVIDIA's own published schedule, and because his suggested tracking method is testable: watch Taiwan's monthly PCB/CCL supplier revenue for which way the 2027 rack mix (Kyber vs Oberon) actually tilts.**
- **🗄️ The CPU-attach ratio, sourced to Intel's CFO rather than to NVDA** (**DAMNANG (Substack)** — "The CPU Bottleneck Trade: Who Actually Gets Paid in the Agentic AI Era?", **2026-04-25**; ⚠️ independent author, NOT a broker — quoting Intel CFO David Zinsner): training-era GPU:CPU was *"roughly 1 CPU per 7 to 8 GPUs"*, inference brings it to *"1 per 3 to 4"*, and agentic AI could move it *"to 1-to-1 or higher."* Same piece marks NVDA's Vera at **88 cores / 176 threads, 1.2TB/s memory bandwidth, 1.5TB capacity**, on a dual-ISA strategy (Grace/Vera on ARM plus a **$400mn Series G into SiFive at a $3.65bn valuation, April 2026** and NVLink Fusion for RISC-V), and notes NVIDIA *"began selling the Vera CPU as a standalone product"* with **CoreWeave as first customer**. ➜ **Historical context for the Vera-CPU-rack customer news dated 08-25 above; the attach-ratio range is the useful part and it is Intel's number, not NVIDIA's.**
**🆕🔴🔴 2026-08-25 — THE DE-SPEC DEBATE GETS ITS FIRST HARD CONFIGURATION TABLE, A DECISION DEADLINE, AND A MOTIVE — AND [[SAMSUNG]] IR SAYS IT IS NOT HAPPENING.** This is the sharpest live contradiction on the page and it should resolve inside 1-1.5 months.

**The bear side (three independent sources, same day).** Jefferies' Asia TMT desk: *"Semianalysis have been talking about a de-spec from Nvidia for months and **we are picking up similar checks but nothing has been decided** — they are looking into different options at the moment. They are now talking about **Rubin Ultra shipping with 192GB of HBM8 8-hi**… that would indeed be a big downgrade."* Their Taiwan checks (Jefferies Asia TMT sales · Conor O'Mara, 2026-08-25):
- *"NVDA and memory vendors are working on **different de-spec scenarios, including 4e 8hi, 4 12/8hi and others**."*
- 🔴 *"Although not yet decided, NVDA and memory vendors **have to make the decision very fast, maybe in the next 1-1.5 months**, because when changing memory spec **a lot of components and rack design need to be changed as well**."*
- *"Reducing memory content would have a **huge impact to the chip and rack performance for Rubin Ultra**, so it is not the only option. **Memory vendors may bring the de-spec pressure to second or third tier customers instead.**"*
- *"One thing we can confirm is **HBM supply will still be in serious shortage in 2027**."*

**TrendForce, same day, same direction:** since 3Q26 NVDA has expanded Rubin Ultra HBM evaluations **beyond the original 12-Hi HBM4e to include 8-Hi HBM4e, 12-Hi HBM4 and 8-Hi HBM4, final configuration undecided**; the driver is **expected 2027 DRAM shortages limiting HBM wafer allocation** plus **uncertainty on 12-Hi HBM4e validation timing and yield ramp**; *"Rubin Ultra's primary goal is **higher I/O speed**, while maximizing GPU shipment volume is a secondary objective"*; successful HBM4e MP could take Rubin Ultra I/O to **14-16 Gbps vs Rubin's 8-11.7 Gbps**, but a delay caps it at **11-12 Gbps via HBM4 optimisation**. It also notes de-spec has ALREADY happened elsewhere: **CSPs and server OEMs reduced RDIMM capacities in 1H26, and NVDA HALVED SOCAMM CAPACITY in Vera Rubin Superchip modules due to expected LPDDR5X shortages through 2027.** **HBM bit shipments +50-60% y/y in 2027, still below demand growth.**

**The configuration table Jefferies circulated (attributed to SemiAnalysis):**

| | Rubin | Rubin Ultra 1st ver | Rubin Ultra 2nd ver |
|---|---|---|---|
| HBM type | HBM4 12-Hi | HBM4 8-Hi | HBM4e 8-Hi |
| Core die | 24Gb | 24Gb | 32Gb |
| Density / cube | 36Gb | 24Gb | 32Gb |
| **Density / GPU** | **288GB** | **192GB** | **256GB** |
| GPUs / system | 72 | 576 | 576 |
| **HBM / system** | **20.7TB** | **110.6TB** | **147.5TB** |

Corpus corroboration with the *mechanism*: *"Rubin Ultra will carry **192GB of HBM4 8-hi** — not only a big downgrade from the originally previewed **1TB** Rubin Ultra, but even **below the standard Rubin's 288GB**. Why cut to 1/5? **(1) the original 4-die Rubin Ultra plan was cancelled, so HBM stacks fall to 8; (2) stack height 16-hi → 8-hi; (3) HBM4 (24Gb dies) instead of the denser HBM4E (32Gb dies)** — though an 8-hi HBM4E upgrade could still come later"* (@QQ_Timmy, corpus, 2026-08-25). @zephyr_z9 adds the offset: *"they are **blowing up the scale-up world size** to compensate for lower HBM per GPU"* (corpus, 2026-08-25).

🔴 **THE MOTIVE, stated plainly by the desk that is most bullish on memory:** *"Nvidia has a **massive memory bill for next year, over $200bn**. For Vera Rubin **close to 80% of its BOM is memory related**, and [[GOOG]] for one is not happy paying a 75% margin on it. For its [[MEDIATEK]] TPUs it's going to **buy the HBM directly**. Nvidia needs to control its memory costs to protect its sales and earnings **as pressure mounts for them to remove HBM from the BOM and allow hyperscalers to buy memory directly**"* (Jefferies Asia TMT sales · Conor O'Mara, 2026-08-25). The same desk has moved its HBM price assumption from **$18/GB (Sherman's earlier marketing-trip number) to $30/GB**, *"implying another **$1m increase in the rack price** just on higher HBM content."*
⚠️⚠️ **THREE BASIS WARNINGS, do not merge these figures.** (1) *"~80% of BOM is memory related"* is a **desk assertion with no bill-of-materials shown** and is **NOT the same denominator** as BofA's *"DRAM 12.7% of rack price vs 12.1%"* (logged 08-24, a ~60bp GM headwind) or the *"memory is 40-50% of BUILD COST"* figure carried elsewhere on this wiki. **All three are different denominators; the page keeps them separate and does not net them.** (2) **$30/GB is a Jefferies desk assumption, not a transacted price.** (3) The **$200bn memory bill is a Jefferies estimate**, not an NVDA disclosure.

**🔴 THE OTHER SIDE, from the company that would have to supply the de-spec:** [[SAMSUNG]] IR, in a BofA-hosted group meeting on the SAME DAY, said *"DRAM supply remains tight but **still no HBM de-spec for high-end GPUs**"* (BofA / Simon Woo, 2026-08-25). And [[AMD]]'s Lisa Su *"said AMD would be **flexible on HBM configurations** for clients based on specific workloads"* (Jefferies, 2026-08-25) — which is the same flexibility framed as a feature rather than a cut. **JPM's Asia Tech Tour arrives at a third reading: "memory content cuts were caused by INSUFFICIENT MEMORY SUPPLY more so than performance-downgrade intent"** (JPM · Jay Kwon, 2026-08-25), with the Asia server food chain *"even exploring **4Hi HBM designs** for future ASIC/GPU configurations"* (JPM · Gokul Hariharan, 2026-08-25). ➤ **Resolution test: the Rubin Ultra HBM configuration must be frozen within ~1-1.5 months per Jefferies. Whichever way it lands, one of these two sources is wrong on the record.**

**🆕🔴 2026-08-25 — MS INITIATES ON NVDA *CREDIT* AT NEUTRAL, AND SIZES THE OFF-BALANCE-SHEET STACK.** (MS Credit Research · Lindsay Tyler, via MS TMT · Thomas Wigg, 2026-08-25) *"Balance-sheet strength is becoming a strategic AI financing tool, but also adding new risks. **Over $1 trillion of guided GPU/XPU-related ecosystem financing may come via creative structures.**"*
- **~$200bn of all-in exposure forecast by CY28-end**, including **~$170bn of adjustments / contingent obligations across leases, PORTS-Pike, the $500bn RVS and the revenue-sharing model.**
- CY28E metrics still strong against that: **~0.4x leverage, >100% FCF-to-debt; ~0.7x and ~15% under plateaued growth.** MS's FY29/CY28 framework implies **>$1tn of debt capacity vs S&P's 1.5x downgrade threshold.**
- 🔴 **"Trades more like BBB than AA after recent widening"; CDS ~25bp wide of similarly-rated hyperscalers.** Corroborated on the tape: *"NVDA [CDS] at record wide every single day now"* (@zerohedge, corpus, 2026-08-25).
**Companion framing from the WSJ the same week:** NVDA is *"using financial engineering — **up to $230bn in lease backstops and residual-value guarantees (including $105bn for an [[OPENAI]] lease and up to $125bn for Wall Street financing deals)**, plus customer-of-last-resort deals and equity stakes in smaller cloud players"* — with the explicit **Lucent vendor-financing analogy** (WSJ via JPM · Joshua Meyers, 2026-08-25). ⚠️ **The $230bn (WSJ) and ~$200bn all-in CY28 (MS) are different constructions of an overlapping exposure — they are not additive.**

**🆕 2026-08-25 — POSITIONING IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE SETUP.** Active long-only funds **sold $44.2bn of semiconductors globally last month** amid concern over the durability of the AI investment cycle, rotating into Telecoms; *"AI-related sectors [are] increasingly UNDER-OWNED"* even as **TSMC, Samsung, ASML and META remain among the largest active overweights globally** (BofA strategy · Nigel Tupper, relayed by Brian Fenske, 2026-08-25). BofA's Vivek Arya: fundamentals strong, but **elevated positioning, higher rates and AI-financing concerns drive near-term de-risking; a −10% SOX pullback would restore its historical pre-AI valuation discount vs the SPX**; SOX at **20x forward P/E while growing EPS 3x the SPX**; and on NVDA specifically he flags the opportunity to lift **cash returns from 50% of FCF to >75%, an [[AAPL]] post-2012 playbook** (BofA, 2026-08-25). **Raymond James raised its NVDA PT to $352 from $330, Strong Buy** (@StockMKTNewz, corpus, 2026-08-25).

- **🆕 Practitioner read-through — NVIDIA is still the best balanced rack today, but background inference weakens the value of its most differentiated latency feature (Invest Like the Best EP488; Sail Research founder/CEO Neil Movva, 2026-08-25).** Movva, a former NVIDIA GPU/kernel engineer and now an interested inference-provider founder, says NVIDIA remains the current leader for both minimum latency and throughput: NVLink is effectively mandatory when tensor-parallel inference must minimize latency, NVL72 turns the rack into the programming unit, and NVIDIA's software, supply relationships and strategic chip allocation compound the advantage. His structural caveat is workload segmentation. Long-running background agents can accept slower generation and tail-latency spikes, allowing larger batches and heterogeneous chips chosen on FLOPS-per-dollar rather than interconnect; in that segment, "there are no bad chips, only bad pricing." - **BACKFILL / HISTORICAL BASE RATE — how the GB200 NVL72 rack-scale ramp actually went (SemiAnalysis "H100 vs GB200 NVL72 Training Benchmarks — Power, TCO and Reliability Analysis; Software Improvement Over Time", 2025-08-20):** _an August-2025 source added on 2026-07-24 as historical structure — it supersedes nothing on this page and is NOT in the current intra-quarter table. Its value is as the only independent record of a rack-scale ramp curve, i.e. the base rate against which to judge the Vera Rubin ramp._ **Economics at the time:** GB200 NVL72 rack **$3.1M ($3.9M all-in per rack)** vs an H100 server at **~$190k (~$250k all-in)** — **capex/GPU 1.6–1.7x and TCO ~1.6x the H100**, so the rack had to be at least 1.6x faster just to break even; GB200 1200W/chip vs H100 700W. **The curve is the point:** perf/TCO vs H100 was **still below 1.0x in May-2025, reached 1.5x by July-2025, and was projected to 2.7x within 3–6 months** — i.e. a rack-scale platform can ship materially *behind* the prior generation on delivered economics and close the gap almost entirely on software inside two quarters. On DeepSeek 670B BF16, tok/s/GPU went **+30% (May-25) → 2.5x (Jul-25) → projected 4.7x (Dec-25)** at 42.0% MFU, cost/M tokens **$0.684 → $0.307** vs H100's $0.468, and a 670B pretrain **$4.5M (Jul-25) → $2.5M projected (Dec-25)**; power efficiency 2.2x by Jul-25, projected 4x lower J/token by Dec-25 (a 100MW datacenter trains 4x more tokens). **Reliability was the drag, and it was rack-scale-specific:** GB200 NVL72 **MTBI 1,000–3,000 GPU-days vs H100's 2,000–5,000**, **XID 149 errors traced to NVLink copper-backplane signal integrity**, blast radius **72 GPUs vs 8**, compute-tray swap 1–4h, switch-tray swap 1–4h **and it drains the whole rack**, backplane swap **8–24h** — enough to cut the Llama4 Maverick perf/TCO advantage from ~50% cheaper to only 20–30% cheaper once hot-spare/spare-rack cost was counted. At that point NVL72 racks were used **only for inference, small experiments and dev jobs**, neoclouds were choosing **HGX B200/B300 over NVL72**, and SemiAnalysis's verdict was that "**vanilla B200 is better performance TCO than GB200 NVL72 for pretraining normal sized models**," with NVL72 winning as models scale and RL comes in. Read-through for today's debate: the Blackwell rack generation took roughly two quarters of software to earn its price premium and a further period to fix backplane reliability — a concrete prior for the Rubin/Oberon ramp (which stays in the same NVL72 scale-up domain) and a reminder that early-ramp perf/TCO prints are not the steady state. See also the Amphenol Paladin-HD connector read-through now filed on [APH.md](APH.md). [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/2025_08_20_ENC_H100_vs_GB200_NVL72_Training_Benchmarks_-_Power_TCO_and_Reliability_Analysis_Software_Improvement_Over_Ti.html)
- **BACKFILL / HISTORICAL — ⚠️ DATED 2026-01-01, SEVEN MONTHS OLD: the NVDA-specific content of the CPO book, now read in full (SemiAnalysis · Dylan Patel, Daniel Nishball, Myron Xie and 3 others, "Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) Book — Scaling with Light for the Next Wave of Interconnect", 2026-01-01).** _This note was already cited on the page (Catalysts, "Scale-up / CPO transition"); this is the full-text pass on its NVDA content. **It supersedes nothing and must be read UNDER the newer CPO rows on this page — Lumentum/PhotonCap 07-29, Fubon 07-28 (NPO/CPO doing inter-rack scale-out one generation earlier), MS Charlie Chan 08-10 ("CPO/NPO reserved for NVL576"), COHR's 08-12 "absolutely no push-out," Nutty 08-12, and the Kyber cancellation itself. Where those conflict with what follows, THEY ARE NEWER.**_
  - **The load-bearing claim:** CPO *"will provide some benefit and bring more options to scale-out networking, but it will be **central to scale-up networking**… the main driver of bandwidth increases in scale-up networking for the latter part of this decade and beyond."* The physics: **NVLink today gives 7.2 Tbit/s per GPU, "soon to be 14.4 Tbit/s per GPU in the Rubin generation," but copper is range-limited to two meters at most, "meaning the scale-up domain world size is limited to one or two racks at most."** For calibration, **NVLink 5.0 on Blackwell = 900 GByte/s (7,200 Gbit/s) uni-directional per GPU, 9x the 100 GByte/s (800 Gbit/s) per GPU on the back-end scale-out network.**
  - **🔴 NVDA's stated position at the time, and it is the origin of a line this page still carries: "for scale-up, Nvidia is still pushing forward with COPPER and going to EXTREME LENGTHS to avoid going to optics, EVEN OUT TO 2027 AND 2028."** The GTC-2025 scale-out CPO switches are read as a pipe-cleaner: *"Nvidia's scale-out CPO product launch is serving as a **practice run and pipe-cleaner** for the real high-volume deployment"*, and — because Rubin Ultra's 2027 target ("we think that ends up being late 2027") leaves the supply chain unable to ship tens of millions of CPO endpoints — ***"the Feynman generation appears to be the focal point for CPO injection into the Nvidia ecosystem."*** ➜ **This is where the page's standing "CPO NVSwitch not available until Feynman" risk line comes from. Date it accordingly.**
  - **⚠️ The scale-OUT TCO math, and it is deflationary for the CPO story:** NVDA's Quantum X800-Q3450 (115.2T) uses **72 optical engines at 1.6 Tbit/s, later ~36 at 3.2 Tbit/s at ~$1,000/unit incl. FAUs ⇒ ~$35-40k of OE+ELS BOM per system**, vs **~$72,000** to populate the non-CPO X800-Q3400 with 1.6T twin-port transceivers — **but "if we were to apply a 60% gross margin, optical engine cost to the end buyer would end up at $80k-$90k USD — which is HIGHER cost than the transceiver equivalent."** Net effect on a 3-layer network: **transceiver cost −86%, switch cost +81%, total networking cost −31%, TOTAL CLUSTER COST ONLY −3%**; flattening to two layers gets **networking −46% and cluster −7%**. Power is the same shape — **networking is just 9% of cluster power, so a 23% networking-power saving is 2% of the cluster (48% / 4% on two layers)** — even though at the component level **an 800G DR4 transceiver draws ~16-17W vs ~4-5W per 800G for NVDA's Q3450 optical engine + external laser sources, a 73% reduction** (Meta/Broadcom Bailly measured 65%). Verdict at the time: ***"we do not expect a rapid adoption curve for scale-out CPO systems within hyperscalers in the near term."*** ⚠️ **That verdict is exactly what is now in dispute — COHR's 08-12 "demand pulled in, ship more as fast as possible" vs Jefferies' same-week "pushed out probably to '29." Keep all three, dated.**
  - **The radix point, which is genuinely NVDA-specific: Quantum 3450 = 144 ports of 800G; Spectrum 6800 = 512 ports of 800G, enough to connect 131,072 GPUs on a TWO-layer network, vs Spectrum 6810's 128 ports of 800G (8,192 GPUs).** "High radix in a box" — the shuffle happens inside the switch instead of via patch panels or octopus cables — is the actual selling point, because it lets customers collapse three layers to two.
  - **🔴 THE SERDES CEILING, AND WHY IT IS A MOAT RISK RATHER THAN A COMPONENT STORY: NVLink 5.0 bandwidth is 11x NVLink 1.0, but lane count only went 32 → 36 — "the key driver of scaling has been a 10x increase in SerDes lane speed, from 20G to 200G." NVLink 6.0 STAYS on 200G SerDes and must double LANE COUNT instead, delivered "cleverly by using bi-directional SerDes" (224 Gbit/s transmit + 224 Gbit/s receive sharing one channel) — and "achieving 'true' 448G per lane on copper remains another challenging feat with an uncertain time to market." The consequence, verbatim: *"**For Nvidia, whose NVLink scale up fabric is an important moat, this roadblock could make it easier for competitors such as AMD, and the hyperscalers to catch up.**"*** ⚠️ **Directly upstream of the Aurelion/Lumentum row of 07-29 already on this page ("bi-directional signaling over copper degrades substantially at 448G per lane") — same argument, six months earlier, from a different house.**
  - **Density context: Blackwell has 23.6 Tbit/s of off-package bandwidth ≈ ~0.4 Tbit/s/mm of shoreline density, against UCIe-A's ~10 Tbit/s/mm on an advanced package (~330 Tbit/s off one reticle-length edge)** — the gap CPO plus wide I/O eventually closes. But **"Broadcom and Nvidia are persisting with electrical SerDes on their roadmap despite the advantages a wide interface offers"**, because they must keep designing for copper and expect hybrid co-packaged-copper/CPO to persist, avoiding multiple tape-outs. **Co-packaged COPPER (CPC) is flagged as the likelier practical path to 448G for short-reach in-rack scale-up.**
  - **⚠️ Kyber, as described in January 2026 — and now superseded by events:** the Rubin Ultra rack *"can scale up to **144 GPU packages (576 GPU dies)**. This rack is **4x denser** than the already dense GB200/300 NVL72 rack."* **Kyber was subsequently cancelled/replaced (MS NDR recap 07-14; Fubon 07-28 and the 08-03 primary). Retained because the 576-compute-die target SURVIVED the cancellation and is what the replacement rack is being designed to hit** — so the density ambition this note documents is still live even though the vehicle is not.
  - **NVDA's CPO supply chain, named — the part of the note nothing else on this page covers.** **Optical engines: TSMC COUPE, with "Nvidia proudly displayed their COUPE optical engines at GTC 2025, and these will be the FIRST COUPE products to ship."** **ELS: the X800-Q3450 uses 18 ELS modules × 8 CW DFB laser chips (~350mW each), and "we expect LUMENTUM to be the SOLE supplier for Nvidia's initial batches of CPO switch shipments, and COHERENT may enter as the SECOND supplier in LATE 2026."** ✅ **That second-source call has since LANDED — cf. - **🆕 A NET-NEW HOUSE ON THIS PAGE — BMO INITIATES AT OUTPERFORM, PT $340, WITH NVDA AS ITS "TOP LARGE-CAP AND OVERALL PICK"** (BMO Capital Markets Corp · Harsh Kumar w/ Wei Mok, CFA, "Initiating at Outperform; Continues to Raise AI Standard", 2026-08-20; px $217.56 Aug-19, total return 57% incl. the $1.00 div). **Base $340 = 25x FY28E EPS $13.56 · upside $475 = 35x forward on "sustained revenue growth of 50% for the foreseeable future" · downside $162 = 12x forward "for lack of growth" if AI capex slows.** Model: revenue **$215.9bn → $396.8bn → $595.7bn** (FY26A/27E/28E), EPS **$4.76 → $8.97 → $13.56**, GM **71.2% → 74.9% → 75.2%**, OpM **63.5% → 66.0% → 66.9%**, FCF **$112.6bn → $260.9bn → $386.1bn**, FY28E capex **$11.9bn**, P/E **45.7x → 24.2x → 16.0x**. ➤ **TWO THINGS TO NOTE AGAINST WHAT THIS PAGE ALREADY HOLDS, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. (1) The $340 base is above every live house PT here except Tigress's $425, and it lands exactly on the Barron's/Al Root bull-ladder MIDPOINT of $340 derived three months earlier from semi-multiple reversion — two unrelated methods, one number. (2) The ESTIMATES ARE NOT AGGRESSIVE; they are Morgan Stanley's. ✅ **AND THE COMPARISON IS GENUINELY LIKE-FOR-LIKE, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT USABLE AS EVIDENCE: both houses sit on NVDA's FY-JAN fiscal basis over the SAME periods (BMO FY26A/FY27E/FY28E against MS 26/27/28e), and the EPS lines are matched non-GAAP-to-non-GAAP — BMO's non-GAAP EPS against MS's CONSENSUS-METHOD EPS, deliberately NOT against MS's ModelWare series. No period, calendarisation or basis adjustment is required, so the residual really is the multiple.** BMO FY27E/FY28E revenue $396.8bn/$595.7bn vs MS ModelWare $393bn/$599bn (**+1.0% / −0.6%**); BMO EPS $8.97/$13.56 vs MS consensus-method $8.98/$13.15 (**−0.1% / +3.1%**). ➤🔴 **THE CONCLUSION, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO INFERENCE FROM THE ADJACENT NUMBERS: NVDA'S PRICE-TARGET DISPERSION ON THIS PAGE IS A MULTIPLE DISPUTE, NOT AN ESTIMATE DISPUTE. Two houses agree on revenue and EPS to within ~3% across two fiscal years on an identical basis, and still differ by $52 of price target — because one pays 25x on the out-year and the other ~22x. Any future PT move on this name should therefore be interrogated as a re-rating argument first and an estimate-revision argument second.** So the $52 of PT above MS comes ENTIRELY FROM THE MULTIPLE (25x vs ~22x on the out-year), not from the numbers — which is Arcuri's "nobody cares anymore about 27, it's all about 28" argument expressed as a target rather than as a complaint, and it is the cleanest evidence on this page that the NVDA PT dispersion is a MULTIPLE dispute, not an estimate dispute.** On the business, BMO's demand section is a supply section: systems "sold out for the next 12-plus months," and "demand is not the primary constraint on growth today. Instead, the main challenge is for NVDA to procure memory and manufacturing capacity for its NVL72 AI systems" (~1.3mn components per rack); revenue split roughly evenly hyperscaler/CSP vs ACIE; reasoning models needing "up to 100x to 1000x more tokens"; and the digital-twin/AV/robotics legs explicitly "still several years away" and NOT in the estimates. **Nothing on this page is superseded — there was no prior BMO rating, PT or estimate to move to Changelog.** [Source](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/BMO_-_NVDA_Initiating_at_Outperform_Continues_to_Raise_AI_Standard_1.html)
- **Bull-case math vs the "AI bubble" search-trend risk (Barron's, two issues):** the bull case rests on cheap-multiple-on-huge-EPS-growth arithmetic that shows up across three separate Barron's pieces: (1) "Rally in Chips" (Adam Levine, 2026-06-01 issue): EPS grew **$0.33 (FY23) → $4.77 (FY26)**; Street sees **$12.37 by FY28**, putting the stock at **17x P/E** on that basis, with a **PEG <0.6x** (17x P/E ÷ 0.28 PEG per Barron's table) vs the S&P 500's ~1.0x. BofA's Vivek Arya "estimates Nvidia has a durable 70% share of the AI chip market." (2) "It's Not Too Late to Buy Into Nvidia's AI Growth Story" (Al Root, 2026-05-18 issue): the stock trades at **~24x NTM earnings, a 25% discount to its own historical valuation and 5% below the SOX index** — despite normally carrying a 40% premium to SOX; "since the start of 2025, Nvidia has trailed the index by more than 70 percentage points." Root's bull-case ladder: 26x avg-semi multiple → **$290**; reversion to historical premium-to-sector multiple → **$390**; midpoint **$340** (a 50% gain from the then-current level). (3) The explicit **risk flag** in the same Root piece: Google searches for "AI bubble" are **up ~400% y/y (peaking in November)**, and NVDA must beat sales-growth estimates of ~80% to satisfy the Street given an average beat of only ~3% over the prior 3 quarters — i.e. the search-trend/sentiment risk is rising exactly as the bar to beat stays high. Gavin Baker (CIO, Atreides, in the 2026-06-01 issue) frames the read-through skeptically across the sector: "The multiples cannot all be accurate... You have memory makers at low-to-mid-single-digit P/Es, you have Nvidia at a low P/E, you have other accelerator companies at reasonable multiples" — i.e. either NVDA is mispriced cheap or the "reasonable" multiples elsewhere (Cerebras ~280x 2027E per the same issue's Trader column, vs NVDA's sub-17x 2027 P/E) are the anomaly (Barron's, 2026-05-18 / 2026-06-01 issues).
- **Hyperscaler-vs-neocloud segment-reporting narrative fight:** the new disclosure format is itself contested. Bulls read the 47%→55% hyperscaler share shift (Barron's/Levine, 2026-05-25) as evidence of *broadening* demand — ACIE (neoclouds/enterprise/sovereign) is a large, still-underappreciated second growth leg, per Huang's own framing that it's "poorly understood." Bears read the same data the other way: hyperscaler revenue growth (+115% y/y) now **outpaces** the smaller-customer segment (+74% y/y) even as Huang told the Street "we should be growing faster than hyperscale capex" — Barron's calls this "a key point of concern for investors," and the stock's ~3% two-day post-print drop despite the beat is the market's verdict on that specific tension (Barron's/Adam Levine, 2026-05-25). Tigress Research (Strong Buy, PT $425 @ $214.86, 2026-05-27) sits at the bull extreme of the PT range: "Nvidia continues to be the core infrastructure engine of the artificial-intelligence factory era... unmatched full-stack technology leadership and surging AI capital expenditure" (Barron's Research Reports excerpt, 2026-06-01 issue).

  - **THE BULL / ENABLING READ (Barclays · Ross Sandler + Tom O'Malley, "Charts Worth A Look: Unpacking AI Infrastructure 'Backstop 101'", 2026-08-13 — industry views U.S. Internet **POSITIVE**, U.S. Semis & Semicap **NEUTRAL**):** *"The AI build-out is heading in a new direction with **upwards of $1T in new compute financing backstopped by Nvidia and Broadcom**. This new approach allows major buyers of AI compute (AI labs) to take more control of their business models, at a time when hyperscaler capex is approaching limits."* Barclays dates the stage change to two events — *"the huge announcements from both **Nvidia (this Monday)** and **Broadcom (XPU on June 9th)**."* **The limits argument, quantified: hyperscaler capex has borne $1.5 trillion since 2023 (through '26), with several trillion more in coming years; the hyperscaler "funding gap" — operating cash flow less capex — could exceed $200B in '27; and the industry has natural limits around debt levels and power agreements that "we seem to be approaching… in '27."** [[GOOG]]'s equity raise — its first since IPO — is cited as the milestone marking it. ➜ **On this read the backstop is an enabling structure that EXTENDS the cycle past a hyperscaler-balance-sheet ceiling, and NVDA is the agent of the extension.**
  - **THE SCEPTIC READ (Ash & Seed Press · Shanaka Anslem Perera, "THE CONTINUITY STACK: NVIDIA Did Not Raise $500 Billion. Wall Street Is Financing the Right to Keep AI Billing.", 2026-08-18 — ⚠️⚠️ **AN INDEPENDENT SUBSTACK AUTHOR WITH NO RATING, NO PRICE TARGET AND NO MODEL. The ingest router tagged this file's broker as "Goldman" — THAT IS FALSE, and instructively so: Goldman Sachs is NAMED IN THE BODY as one of the six financing partners. Do not lend this piece broker authority.**):** the central claim is definitional — that the $500bn *"was not revenue, committed capital, a single fund, or money assigned to one customer,"* and that the **memoranda of understanding remain subject to final agreements**. His framing: ***"$500 Billion Is a Market Design, Not a Cash Balance"*** — the platforms mobilise third-party capital over time and *"create neither $500 billion of orders nor cash at NVIDIA's disposal. Each project still requires underwriting, documentation, funding, construction, power, acceptance, and a paying customer."* What the announcement actually does, on his account, is that *"NVIDIA is trying to make that process repeatable."* On the residual-value leg: **NVDA has said it may provide residual-value support for selected projects, and Perera characterises a "possible 25 percent support" as *"an undisclosed recovery instrument"*** — ⚠️ **record the 25% as the AUTHOR'S characterisation of size/terms that are NOT public, explicitly not as a disclosed NVDA term** (cf. the MS/Moore 08-11 line already on this page, which treats the 25% as the thing to be tested deal-by-deal). His thesis line: *"NVIDIA is not merely supporting the resale price of aging chips. It is supporting the fixed infrastructure that allows successive generations of chips to remain installed, powered, and billable"* — hence the title; the unpriced asset is *"the right to keep billing."*
  - ⚠️ **THE MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, AND IT IS THE AUTHOR'S OWN — carry it so the page does not overclaim in either direction: maximum exposure, commitment, designed capacity, fair value, expected loss, revenue and funded notional are DISTINCT MEASURES; his references to circularity, concentration, wrong-way risk and financing dependence are *"analytical descriptions"* and allege no misconduct.** What would settle it, in his words: *"Executed term sheets can expose support and price. Operating data can expose the cash. A default can expose the recovery."* ➜ **This is the same falsifiability test the page already runs through the 10-Q partner-lease-guarantee line ($3.5bn today) — logged as convergent, from a non-broker source.** [Barclays](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/Barclays_U_S_Internet_Semiconductors_Charts_Worth_A_Look_Unpacking_AI_Infrastructure_Backstop_101_.html) · [Ash & Seed](../relat%C3%B3rios%20bons/cont_stack.html)

Because **CPO NVSwitch is not available until Feynman**, NVDA has no proven way to grow the scale-up world size for Rubin Ultra — a scale-up-roadmap gap that opens the door for **AMD MI500X** and **GOOGL TPUv8i 'Broadfly'** (see Current state + Risks).

NVDA's near-term CPO is on scale-out (Quantum/Spectrum); first big scale-up CPO ramp is modeled on Amazon's Trainium4, i.e. a competitor's platform — watch whether NVDA brings scale-up CPO into Rubin Ultra/Kyber.

## Risks
- **Demand sustainability / AI-capex ROI** — hyperscaler + neocloud FCF and financing dependence (Crisafulli, Chanos).
- **Customer concentration** — top-5 cloud/hyperscalers ~50%+ of DC revenue; large direct/indirect customer exposure. 🆕 **The sharpest available statement of the structural version (SemiAnalysis · Kan/Wang/Patel, "Korea's Trillion-Dollar Sovereign AI Investment", 2026-09-01 — ⚠️ independent research house, not a broker): because *"selling frontier tokens at API prices is the highest ROI use case of incremental compute,"* [[ANTHROPIC]] + [[OPENAI]] take a rising share of net-new GW, so NVDA is *"currently on track for a world where they only have 2 real customers… maybe 7 if you include the hyperscalers,"* and *"all 7 customers except SpaceX are actively trying to build their own XPUs to cannibalize Nvidia's margins."* ➜ That is the risk-side reading of why NVDA is funding open-source models and sovereign AI: customer diversification, not incremental TAM.**
- **Supply concentration** — TSMC (N3/N2 + CoWoS), HBM (SK Hynix/Samsung/Micron), advanced packaging are gating; "supply-constrained throughout life of Vera Rubin."
- **Competition** — custom ASIC the sharpest structural threat: GOOG TPUv7, **AWS Trainium3/4** (open-sourcing software to attack CUDA; AWS Trainium3 Deep Dive, 2025-12-04), AVGO/MRVL merchant ASIC, AMD MI400/MI450X (OpenAI ~26GW deal + equity rebate), inference-specialist silicon. JPM ASIC volume CAGR 32% vs GPU 7% (2025-28); UBS ASIC ~25-30% of accelerator TAM long-term.
- **Scale-up roadmap gap for Rubin Ultra (new, 2026-07-06)** — with the **Kyber NVL144 delayed 12+ months to 2028** (PCB-midplane manufacturability), **NVL576 delayed/small-volume**, **NVL72x2 cancelled**, and **CPO NVSwitch not available until Feynman**, NVDA currently has no proven solution to expand the scale-up world size for Rubin Ultra — a window for **AMD MI500X** and **GOOGL TPUv8i 'Broadfly'** to gain scale-up advantages (SemiAnalysis, via CNBC & MS TMT, 2026-07-06). Bear-ish nuance for the scale-up leg of the moat, distinct from the merchant-ASIC-units debate above.
- **Downstream (rack) integration, not upstream silicon, is now the named gate on the next generation (new, 2026-08-03)** — per Arthur's ODM checks on the Fubon call, the goal of **144 GPUs per rack is fixed ("that's for sure")** but the unsolved problems are **heat dissipation, cable design, and the power density of existing datacenters** — because GPU-to-rack connection is **still cable-based**, with a single rack potentially reaching **~1 million watts**. Verbatim: **"Nvidia face a lot of problem, not only from upstream, it's from downstream."** Hon Hai is still submitting competing **two-rack and four-rack proposals**, and the **new Rubin Ultra rack design is not expected until ~the December quarter of 2027** while Rubin racks start shipping this December quarter — against Shang's warning that **"we are already in August, so the timeline is very, very tight to enter production for Ruben Ultra."** This is a distinct risk from the packaging/CoWoS and scale-up-world-size risks above: those are foundry problems, this one sits at the ODM and in customer datacenters (existing power density is a *customer* constraint NVDA cannot engineer away). Complements the page's power ladder (JPM: VR Ultra ~1.5MW / 800V HVDC) by giving the ODM-side reason the design is unfinished. (Fubon · Sherman Shang / Arthur (hosted by Jefferies), 2026-08-03)
- **🆕 Time-to-power / approved-MW scarcity, now with a regulatory trigger and a price (Bernstein · Gautam Chhugani, "AI Infra/miners: Texas data center audit to drive more MW scarcity", 2026-08-04, read-through — subject is the miner/AI-infra cohort):** **Governor Abbott has directed the PUCT and ERCOT to audit ALL data-center projects in ERCOT's interconnection process, and ERCOT has PAUSED the "Batch Zero" review that was due to publish classification results on 2026-08-07** (queue **474 GW of REQUESTS**, data centers ~90% of new requests — ⚠️ **a queued/requested figure, not energised / IT-load / facility GW; see `_meta/assumptions.md`**). Bernstein: the audit **"throttles speculative data center pipeline and makes genuine sites with development history more valuable"** — **already-approved MW re-rate upward and time-to-power lengthens for new builds**, which is a revenue-*timing* risk for GPUs that need energised halls. The price of it is already visible in Bernstein's Exhibit 2: **NVDA's contract with IREN yields ~$15mn per IT MW vs ~$10mn under Microsoft's contract with the same counterparty (~50% higher; on a gross-MW basis ~$14mn vs ~$11mn — ⚠️ two different bases, do not mix)** — i.e. **NVDA is paying up for scarce approved megawatts.** IREN is not a wiki-covered name. See [themes/ai-datacenter-power](themes/ai-datacenter-power.md).
- **China / export controls** — China DC compute zeroed in guidance; geopolitical and licensing risk.
- **Valuation/sentiment** — "funding short" status; UBS view that multiple expansion is exhausted (~20x buy-side out-year EPS); correlation to decelerating y/y growth as comps peak ~FQ2.
- **"AI bubble" search-trend / sentiment risk** — Google searches for "AI bubble" up ~400% y/y (peaked November); stock trailed the SOX index by >70pp since start of 2025 despite normally trading at a 40% premium to it; bar to beat (~80% sales growth) stays high vs an average ~3% beat over the prior 3 quarters (Barron's/Al Root, 2026-05-18).
- **Hyperscaler-growth-mix optics** — hyperscaler DC revenue (+115% y/y) now outpacing the ACIE/smaller-customer segment (+74% y/y) even as management told the Street NVDA "should be growing faster than hyperscale capex" — stock fell ~3% over two days post-Q1-print despite the beat on this specific tension (Barron's/Adam Levine, 2026-05-25).
- **HBM/memory-wall structural dependency** — Nvidia commands the "lion's share" of HBM demand through 2027 (Rubin Ultra pushes per-GPU HBM to 1TB), and is likely the most profitable HBM vendor in the world by capturing margin on HBM shipped inside its accelerators — but that same concentration is the supply chain's single point of stress (SK Hynix/Samsung/Micron allocation, HBM4 base-die-first risk, pricing step-ups) already flagged above (SemiAnalysis "Scaling the Memory Wall", 2025-08-11).

**Síntese do quarter:** *the print settled the numbers and pushed every open debate one level deeper rather than closing it.* **Demand and supply are both confirmed — +70% on a supply-constrained basis, a >$2tn industry backlog, and input availability now functioning as a competitive moat. The margin shock is confirmed and management pre-committed the trough (71-72% in FQ4) rather than letting it leak out quarterly.** The two genuinely unresolved items are **(1) the counterparty-credit concentration management itself sized at ~25% of FY28 revenue, whose P&L footprint is already visible in a 45→60-day DSO jump and a +$24.6bn AR build, and (2) whether the binding 2027 constraint is still memory or has migrated to ABF substrates / PCB / CCL / T-glass, where — unlike HBM — no de-spec lever exists.** ⚠️ **The de-spec question that dominated print eve was never asked on the call, and was answered elsewhere in the same 48 hours: [[SKHYNIX]] on the record, a named already-executed high-end cut at [[GOOG]] TPUv8, and NVDA's own NVHBM.**

**Síntese do quarter:** _six datapoints in, and the window's shape has already changed from the one the print framed._ **Revenue is not the question: management has put a supply-set floor of +~70% under FY28. What the first week of flow has done is (a) SETTLE the commitments argument with the company's own table — $279bn is a row, $366bn is the total, and there is a SECOND $56bn table plus $108.5bn of guarantees that no broker note on this page had carried; (b) DEGRADE the quality of the gross-margin line, because MS's channel work says the rack LPDDR5 content was halved and moved to consignment so it no longer passes through NVDA's P&L — the GM% is flattered, gross-profit DOLLARS are the honest series; and (c) CONVERGE two independent sources (Jefferies' primary conference note and DAMNANG's arithmetic) on the same reading of the HBM de-spec — a supply response that stretches a constrained die pool into MORE accelerator shipments, not a demand signal, with the memory makers' revenue landing at 81.5-98% of plan rather than falling with the bit count.** ⚠️ **Three things are still open and none of them is revenue: (1) whether the 71-72% FQ4 trough holds once you strip the LPDDR5 de-consolidation; (2) whether "executed price increases" stick with customers the vendor is simultaneously financing; and (3) the Rubin Ultra spec itself — Jefferies, MS and DAMNANG all say the final configuration is UNSET, and MS adds that the Kyber boards have been re-architected. Nobody on this page can confirm 8-Hi.** _The bear case has moved off the income statement and onto the balance sheet, and the balance sheet just got $164bn bigger in disclosed exposure._

**🆕🔴 Síntese — UPDATE 2026-09-01: the window's first genuinely BEARISH read of the +70% guide arrives, and it does not attack the number — it attacks its COMPOSITION.** Nine of the ten rows above treat +70% as the bull event. **Morgan Stanley Asia · Charlie Chan (Asia memory webcast, 2026-09-01) decomposes it: if 10-15% of the 2027 guide is price increase passing memory cost through, implied compute VOLUME growth is ~50-60% — which is exactly MS Asia's pre-existing assumption, so *"that 70% doesn't really give us a kind of further upside for our numbers for… capacity whatsoever."*** ➜ **Two consequences for how this page should be read for the rest of the quarter. (1) THE REVENUE ROW AND THE MARGIN ROW ARE THE SAME EVENT. The pass-through that inflates the top line is the memory cost the GM guide absorbs, and [[SKHYNIX]] pricing is now sized independently — SemiAnalysis (09-01) has NVDA's 2027 HBM4 at ~$3.0-3.3/Gb, a *"~70% YoY"* step-up but 15-25% BELOW what [[AMD]]/[[AVGO]]/AWS/[[GOOG]] pay, and materially below Samsung's +98% / [[MU]]'s +89%. Within a CPX rack, each group of 64 forms a rack module comprising **eight compute trays (eight CPX GPUs per tray) and one switch tray**."* (3) Fabric — *"**NVLink is used ONLY for scale-up among the eight CPX GPUs within each tray, with 1–1.5 TB/s of NVLink bandwidth per CPX (vs. 3.6 TB/s per Rubin)**. Inter-tray scale-out within each rack module runs over **Spectrum-6 Ethernet using ALL-COPPER L1 links**. Across rack modules, scale-out is handled by each module's **Spectrum-6 switch over OSFP OPTICAL links**."* (4) *"CPX must be **paired with Vera Rubin NVL72**."*
➜ **THREE CONSEQUENCES THIS PAGE SHOULD CARRY SEPARATELY. (a) MEMORY: a prefill part specced on GDDR7 is now specced on 168GB of HBM4 in 1Q27 production — incremental HBM content that was in nobody's 2027 model days ago, because the program was believed cancelled. See [themes/hbm-memory](themes/hbm-memory.md). (b) NETWORKING: NVLink is deliberately DE-EMPHASISED (1-1.5 TB/s vs 3.6) and Spectrum-6 Ethernet does the scale-out — copper inside the rack module, OSFP optical only across modules. That is an NVIDIA-captured networking socket and a copper-first architecture at the module level; read it against the CPO timing debate rather than as CPO demand. (c) ARCHITECTURE: a standalone prefill rack that must be paired with VR NVL72 is DISAGGREGATED INFERENCE productised — the same direction Barclays describes below, and the opposite of [[OPENAI]]'s Jalapeño choice.** ⚠️ **Single independent source, checks-based. Kuo has a strong supply-chain record but this is not company-confirmed and the program's status changed once already.** |

| **08-09** | 🔴🔴 **SemiAnalysis — "Ultra-High Interactivity on NVIDIA GPUs? TileRT InferenceX." A SOFTWARE RESULT THAT DEFENDS NVIDIA'S WEAKEST FLANK — and quietly cannibalises Nvidia's own LPU line** | produto / competicao | **bull (with one sharp internal contradiction)** | **★ THE SETUP, WHICH IS THE HONEST STATEMENT OF THE GPU'S ONE STRUCTURAL WEAKNESS: "GPUs perform exceptionally well at HIGH THROUGHPUT AND LOW-TO-MEDIUM INTERACTIVITY, but their architecture is LESS SUITED FOR ULTRA-LOW-LATENCY inference… The gap comes from LATENCY RATHER THAN BANDWIDTH." An 8-GPU HGX B200 has 64 TB/s aggregate HBM bandwidth and GLM-5 at NVFP4 needs only ~21GB of active-parameter traffic per token, implying a roofline of 3,047 TOKENS/S/USER at batch 1 — "in practice, GPUs come NOWHERE CLOSE to this limit," because kernel launch/teardown and synchronisation dominate below ~1ms TPOT even with CUDA graphs.** 🔴 **AND THE LINE THAT BELONGS IN THE MEMORY DEBATE AS MUCH AS HERE: "although GPU MEMORY BANDWIDTH INCREASES BY ROUGHLY 2–3× EACH GENERATION, MEMORY LATENCY HAS NOT IMPROVED AT ALL… EVEN AS HBM PRICES CONTINUALLY INCREASE."** Cross-file [hbm-memory](themes/hbm-memory.md). **THE RESULT: TileRT statically compiles the entire decode graph into ONE PERSISTENT KERNEL ("a CUDA graph optimizes the LAUNCHING of kernels; TileRT ABOLISHES THE KERNEL AS THE UNIT OF EXECUTION"), with warp- and whole-GPU specialisation (in GLM-5.1's attention layer "GPU 0 becomes a SPARSE INDEXER worker… GPUs 1 through 7 run the MLA workers"). On the InferenceX GLM-5.1 benchmark: at 8k/1k, TileRT hits 340 TOKENS/S/USER ON AN EIGHT-GPU B200 NODE vs a prior best of 181.4 on GB300 NVL72 with NVFP4+MTP (1.9×), and 3.0× the fastest FP8 result (113.6 on B300 with MTP). At 1k/1k, TileRT FP8 reaches 494.2 tok/s/user — 1.9× the best conventional FP4 (256.3) and 3.6× the best conventional FP8 (136.3) — "and TileRT DOESN'T YET HAVE FP4 SUPPORT." End-to-end latency 4.5× better at 1k/1k and 3.0× at 8k/1k, the decode tail being 3.01s vs 6.54s for the best NVFP4+MTP competitor and 18.18s for [[AMD]]'s MI355X.** ⚠️ **READ THE BASIS BEFORE READING THE HEADLINE: this is BATCH SIZE 1, one in-flight request per decode node (v0.1.5), and it is an interactivity result, NOT a throughput or cost-per-token result on its own. The trade is explicit — at 8k/1k the GB300 FP4+MTP point at concurrency 12 delivers ~240 total tok/s/GPU at 154 tok/s/user, while TileRT delivers 160.4 tok/s/GPU at 340 tok/s/user. "TileRT is not just a race car, but MORE LIKE A PRIVATE ROCKET SHIP WITH ROOM FOR JUST ONE PASSENGER."** ✅ **THE TCO NUMBERS, WHICH ARE WHAT MAKE IT A COMMERCIAL RESULT RATHER THAN A BENCHMARK: "At 8k/1k, TileRT reaches 340 tok/s/user while delivering 35.4 output tokens/s per B200. This comes out to $13.56 PER MILLION OUTPUT TOKENS." Against the best FP4 disagg point (GB200 FP4+MTP at concurrency 5, ~176 tok/s/user, $1.86/GB200-hour) at $13.4/M: "TileRT therefore costs ONLY 1% MORE PER TOKEN WHILE DELIVERING 1.9× THE INTERACTIVITY." Against the fastest conventional FP8 (GB300 FP8+MTP, 108 tok/s/user, ~$35/M): "61% CHEAPER PER OUTPUT TOKEN WHILE DELIVERING 3.1× THE INTERACTIVITY."** ⚠️ **The pricing benchmark they choose is a competitor's product tier: "this is MUCH MORE VALUE THAN CLAUDE CODE FAST MODE, UP TO 2.5× THE INTERACTIVITY BUT 2× THE PRICE PER TOKEN" — i.e. the premium fast-mode tiers labs are now selling are being repriced by open-source software running on installed GPUs. See [tokenmaxxing](themes/tokenmaxxing.md).** 🔴 **THE STRATEGIC POINT, AND IT IS THE REASON THIS IS AN NVDA ROW: the fungibility argument. "A GPU POOL IS ONE LIQUID RESOURCE — excellent at prefill, excellent at high-to-medium-batch decode, and NOW SOMEWHAT CREDIBLY STRONG AT ULTRA-INTERACTIVE DECODE, with capacity moving between those roles as a SOFTWARE SCHEDULER DECISION that can follow demand hour by hour. AN ASIC FLEET IS THE OPPOSITE: the ratio of speed-tier capacity to everything else is FIXED IN HARDWARE THE DAY THE PURCHASE ORDER IS SIGNED… Guess wrong with GPUs and you REBALANCE IN SOFTWARE. Guess wrong with dedicated silicon and you either STRAND CAPITAL IN IDLE SPEED MACHINES or TURN AWAY THE EXACT PREMIUM TRAFFIC YOU BOUGHT THEM FOR." The market evidence given: TileRT decode is already in production behind Xiaomi's MiMo V2.5 Pro UltraSpeed and Z.ai's GLM-5.1 HighSpeed, and "NEITHER COMPANY PROCURED A NEW DATAFLOW CHIP. THEY CARVED A SPEED TIER OUT OF THE ACCELERATOR CLUSTER THEY ALREADY RAN… GOOD ENOUGH ON HARDWARE YOU ALREADY OWN TENDS TO BEAT ARCHITECTURALLY PURE ON HARDWARE YOU HAVE TO BUY."** ⚠️⚠️ **THE INTERNAL CONTRADICTION FOR NVIDIA SPECIFICALLY, AND NOBODY IN THE NOTE NAMES IT: the TAM this result attacks is not only [[CEREBRAS]]/Groq/SambaNova's — NVIDIA NOW SELLS INTO IT ITSELF. The note twice refers to "NVIDIA GROQ LPUs" and states that "the SemiAnalysis Accelerator Model has our quarter-by-quarter estimates of NVIDIA LPU30, LPU40, [[CEREBRAS]] WSE-3 & WSE-4 shipments." If TileRT lets a GB200/B200 fleet serve the speed tier at iso-cost, the first casualty inside Nvidia's own book is the LPU line it acquired Groq to own. Logged as an unresolved tension, not as a call.** ⚠️ **THE CEILING IS STILL PHYSICS, AND THE NOTE CONCEDES IT: "Cerebras serves a dense 70B at speeds NO EIGHT-GPU NODE CAN REACH regardless of scheduling: SOFTWARE CAN APPROACH THE HBM ROOFLINE, BUT IT CANNOT RAISE IT." Two candidate designs are in play: **(a) the conservative option — stay on the current Oberon rack, with one system built from four racks connected by traditional scale-out; each Oberon rack holds 144 compute dies, so 4 × 144 = 576**; **(b) a two-rack design Fubon calls "Taycan" — each rack has 144 GPUs × 2 compute dies, with NPO/CPO used for the scale-out connection BETWEEN the two racks and cable retained for scale-up inside each rack.** **Neither is finalised, and Fubon is explicit that it is therefore "difficult to say who will benefit and who will suffer" — it declines to name winners and losers. **Quarter synthesis:** flow **split** — demand/product bulls (Moore Top Pick PT $288, Arya PO $320, Barclays OW $275, Cantor 40 GW) against a growing chorus on **margin/competition** (Redburn HBM +70–80%, JPM ASIC>GPU in '27, Chanos/Crisafulli on sustainability). On Jun-24 two events added pressure to the bear side: (1) **Jalapeño (OpenAI+Broadcom)** — the world's largest lab announced its own inference chip; (2) **GB300 NVL72 firmware bug** (SemiAnalysis): racks need a reboot every 66.5 days. New from 06-27: (3) **A100 spot +20%** — installed base still price-appreciating despite Blackwell ramp, demand is broad; (4) **SambaNova $10B** — inference-ASIC ecosystem gaining VC conviction (mixed for NVDA's inference share); (5) **AI accelerators 11x 2022–26** — structural confirmation of the demand decade thesis. Near-term: hardware-to-software rotation narrative is creating intraday flow pressure but no fundamental shift. Net: demand thesis intact in training, debate intensified on inference share, margin (HBM) and firmware execution. **06-29/30:** Citi makes DRAM/HBM allocation the new ranking metric and puts NVDA #1 (HBM as advantage, not just consignment risk); SemiAnalysis's Accelerator Model sees 2H FY27 DC compute ~20% above consensus with Rubin's ramp back on track post-HBM4 fix; expert calls stay constructive on NVDA's position but flag the CUDA moat eroding (open-source inference engines) and physical-AI/humanoid as a real-but-back-end-loaded TAM. **06-30/07-01:** unit story turns more bullish into 2027 — UBS (Sunny Lin) raises Vera CPU units to 5.5mn in 2027 (from 1.6mn 2026, +57% CoWoS demand) and keeps Rubin at 2.1mn units for 2026 despite a slower Q2 ramp on redesigns; Jefferies/Favuzza (citing SemiAnalysis) sees 2H FY27 DC compute ~20% above consensus on the same post-HBM4-fix Rubin ramp; JPM's Data Center Watch shows GPU rental pricing still rising across all tiers in June and OpenRouter token volume/spend up 70% m/m, a live demand-pull signal; MS (Moore) prefers NVDA on tightening supply/demand even as broader semi inventory sits 33 days above median; the xAI→Anthropic Colossus 1 resale ($1.25bn/month, 220k+ GPUs) reinforces that next-gen compute stays scarce even as older-gen capacity recycles; two AlphaSense expert calls corroborate the moat debate — NVIDIA still dominant today but competitors catching up (ex-AMD manager), and a strong training moat vs rising inference competition from Trainium/AMD/Cerebras (ex-Cerebras/AWS advisor). **07-06 (MS TMT Sales / MS Semis Weekly / SemiAnalysis):** the flow turns two-sided. Bear-ish for the scale-up roadmap — SemiAnalysis (via CNBC & MS TMT) reports the **Kyber NVL144 rack delayed 12+ months to 2028** on PCB-midplane manufacturability, **NVL576 delayed/small-volume**, the **NVL72x2 alternative cancelled**, and **CPO NVSwitch not available until Feynman**, leaving NVDA with no proven way to grow the scale-up world size for **Rubin Ultra** and opening a window for **AMD MI500X** and **GOOGL TPUv8i 'Broadfly'** (an honest competitive-risk nuance, not spun). Offsetting on the demand/capital side: MS/Joe Moore reads the GPU shortage as still binding ("excess demand, not excess supply" — subletting a positive for NVDA share), and SemiAnalysis frames the **>$7T-by-2029 AI-debt market with NVDA as the "central bank"** revenue-guaranteeing neoclouds — bull for buildout continuity, but deepening the circular-financing critique. Net: demand/financing thesis intact; the sharpest new bear is the **scale-up-world-size gap for Rubin Ultra** while CPO/Kyber slip. **07-10 (MS NDR):** Joe Moore's primary post-NDR note reiterates NVDA as MS's Top Pick in semis (PT $288, bull $330/bear $160) and reframes the story around a **new 3-segment growth framework** (AI labs ~20% / traditional hyperscalers ~half / AI-clouds-industrial-enterprise ~half of DC rev), with **both NVDA & AVGO growing 80%+ next year and supply-constrained** (management/MS argue no dramatic ASIC share shift; lowest cost/token frequently NVDA), the **roadmap on track** (Rubin Ultra ships next year — NOT 2028; Kyber replaced by a "better solution"; 800V/optical on schedule — a 3rd corroboration of NVDA's 07-07 denial + Citi's 07-08 IR check), a multi-year memory shortage forcing content trade-offs (LPDDR5/rack halved), and — the newest angle — **50%+ of cash flow now moving to cash return**, positioning NVDA as a "value name" and broadening the NDR to value investors.   🔴 **THE FINDING: a piece of open-source software (TileRT) removes most of the ultra-low-latency deficit that justified an entire class of competing silicon. On the InferenceX GLM-5.1 benchmark an EIGHT-GPU B200 NODE reaches 340 tok/s/user at 8k/1k — 1.9× the previous best of 181.4, which required a 72-GPU GB300 NVL72 with NVFP4+MTP — and 494.2 tok/s/user at 1k/1k with FP8 (3.6× the best conventional FP8), "and TileRT DOESN'T YET HAVE FP4 SUPPORT." Mechanism: the whole decode graph statically compiled into ONE PERSISTENT KERNEL — "a CUDA graph optimizes the LAUNCHING of kernels; TileRT ABOLISHES THE KERNEL AS THE UNIT OF EXECUTION."**
  ✅ **THE COMMERCIAL NUMBER, which is why it is bullish rather than merely interesting: $13.56 PER MILLION OUTPUT TOKENS at 340 tok/s/user versus $13.4 at 176 tok/s/user for the best conventional FP4 point — 1% more cost for 1.9× the interactivity — and 61% CHEAPER than the fastest conventional FP8 endpoint (~$35/M) at 3.1× the interactivity. Benchmarked explicitly against a lab's premium tier: "much more value than CLAUDE CODE FAST MODE, up to 2.5× the interactivity but 2× the price per token."** **Strategic core: "A GPU POOL IS ONE LIQUID RESOURCE… capacity moving between roles as a SOFTWARE SCHEDULER DECISION… AN ASIC FLEET IS THE OPPOSITE: the ratio is FIXED IN HARDWARE THE DAY THE PURCHASE ORDER IS SIGNED." Production proof: Xiaomi MiMo V2.5 Pro UltraSpeed and Z.ai GLM-5.1 HighSpeed, both on clusters they already owned.**
